**Affordable Housing Ordinance (Zoning Code Article 29): inclusionary units and Affordable Housing Impact Fee**
- Agency: City of Redwood City, Housing Services (City Manager's Office) and Community Development
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Rental projects of 20 or more units: 20% affordable (10% moderate, 5% low, 5% very low income). Ownership projects of 20 or more units: 15% moderate income. Projects of 5 to 19 units and nonresidential projects over 5,000 square feet pay the Affordable Housing Impact Fee (Resolution 15462 of 2015; nonresidential rates raised December 20, 2021 to $23.62 per square foot for office, medical office and R&D and $5.91 for hotel, retail, restaurant and services; residential small-project rate reported at about $20 to $25 per square foot, with a temporary 25% reduction for 5 to 19 unit projects that pull vertical permits by June 30, 2027). Fees fund the City's affordable housing NOFA.
- AMI requirement: Rental units restricted at least 55 years, ownership at least 30 years, recorded covenants in first position; fractional units met by an extra unit or in-lieu fee set by Council resolution; 100% affordable projects exempt from the fee.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; fees due before the first building permit. The 2026 San Mateo County multi-city nexus study (Strategic Economics, Redwood City is a participant) may change percentages and fees in 2027.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. Redwood City is the deepest inclusionary program in the county at 20% for rental with a very low income tier, which is why most downtown projects negotiate on-site units rather than pay the fee and why the impact fee fund grows mainly from commercial projects (Elco Yards is expected to pay about $5.8 million in 2026). Alternative compliance plans (off-site, land, conversions) go to Council. The ordinance text is on the City's code host (source, Article 29, Ordinances 1130-375 of 2018, 2498 of 2021, 1130-387 of 2023 and 1130-890 of 2024); fee amounts are from the December 20, 2021 staff report on meetings.redwoodcity.org because redwoodcity.org returns 403 to automated access. ### City of Richmond

- Agency: City of Richmond Community Development Department, Planning Division

- Typical award: Regulatory incentive, not a cash subsidy. **Richmond Inclusionary Housing and Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Ordinance (Richmond Municipal Code Article 15.04.603, readopted 2020) and in-lieu fee**
- Agency: City of Richmond Community Development Department, Housing Division (Jesus Morales, Housing Manager, 510-620-6649) and Planning Division
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to residential and mixed-use projects of 10 or more units. Compliance options: for-sale projects 7% of units at low income or 10% at moderate income; rental projects 9% at very low income or 10% at low income. The in-lieu fee is per square foot and geographically tiered, $0 to $12 per square foot (rental projects south of I-580 and on the Point San Pablo peninsula pay $12 per square foot; market-rate projects north of I-580 are exempt from on-site units and the fee after a 2020 feasibility study); for-sale projects south of I-580 and on Point San Pablo must build units and may not pay the fee. A non-residential affordable housing linkage fee was authorized in the same 2020 update. Collections: $803,055 in-lieu fees in calendar 2020 and $677,194 in 2021. Other alternatives: 10% very low income rental units in a for-sale project, off-site construction, or land dedication yielding at least 10% more units than required.
- AMI requirement: 45-year affordability for for-sale inclusionary units and 55 years for rental units under a recorded Inclusionary Housing Agreement; incentives include the Article 15.04.602 density bonus, clustering of units where a funding source requires it, and smaller or different unit types if at least 5% more affordable units result.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; fee due per the Inclusionary Housing Agreement. Housing Element Program 2.A called for reassessment of the ordinance and linkage fee by first quarter 2024 and any amendments by third quarter 2025, with annual performance reports; confirm with the Housing Division whether amendments were adopted.)
- Layering notes: Richmond's 2020 rewrite deliberately lowered requirements north of I-580 (Hilltop, North Richmond edge) to make market-rate housing feasible, so most inclusionary units and fees come from the south side (Marina Bay, downtown, Point San Pablo). Fees and linkage revenue fund the City Affordable Housing Fund (separate record). Richmond's Rent Program (Measure L, 2016) caps rent increases on pre-1995 multifamily and sets just-cause rules, which affects underwriting of acquisition-rehab deals. The County's Chapter 822-4 inclusionary ordinance does not apply inside Richmond. ci.richmond.ca.us pages for the ordinance redirect to a login page and the Municode host is blocked, so terms were read from the City's adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element (Resolution 7-23, source_url, Appendix C and Appendix G); the $12 per square foot tier was corroborated in the City of Antioch's January 2026 countywide in-lieu fee comparison (Attachment G to the March 10, 2026 Antioch council packet).
- Source: https://www.ci.richmond.ca.us/ArchiveCenter/ViewFile/Item/12751
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

- Agency: City of Richmond as Successor Agency to the Richmond Community Redevelopment Agency, Housing and Community Development (HCD) Division, 450 Civic Center Plaza
- Type: loan

- Layering notes: Richmond's former redevelopment areas (Iron Triangle, Harbour, Hilltop, Nevin) left land assets that the City can contribute to deals; Nevin Plaza Phase II (EAH, 76 units) and the Hacienda Apartments rehabilitation (150 units, CDBG-assisted) are current examples of City-assisted projects. Successor funds stack with HOME, Measure X and the County conduit bond program (county records) and with HACCC project-based vouchers, which now administer the former Richmond Housing Authority voucher program. The Successor Agency web page (https://www.ci.richmond.ca.us/97/Successor-Agency-To-Redevelopment) was opened but is dated (2015-2016 Oversight Board materials); program details were read from the adopted Housing Element (source_url). Audit November 8, 2026: funding_type set to loan; the fund also holds land, so a Richmond deal may receive a land contribution rather than cash. No SB 341 report for Richmond was found online.
- Source: https://www.ci.richmond.ca.us/ArchiveCenter/ViewFile/Item/12751
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of Riverside

**City of Riverside HUD entitlement funds: HOME Infill Residential Development Program and CDBG (FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan)**
- Agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
- Type: loan
- Typical award: FY 2026-27 HUD allocations total $9,050,906: CDBG $2,749,768, HOME $981,735 (of which $883,561 to the Infill Residential Development Program, plus about $200,000 HOME program income), ESG $250,428, HOPWA $5,068,975 (City is the HOPWA EMSA grantee for both Riverside and San Bernardino counties). Recent HOME loans: $1,508,234 Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units), $1,550,443 Mulberry Gardens Family (11 HOME units). HOME-ARP also used ($3,000,000 Mulberry Gardens Senior).
- AMI requirement: HOME: at or below 80% AMI with HOME rent limits; 20-year minimum HOME period for new construction, City typically records 55 years.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: Public notice of funding availability released each December (last one December 2025) for the following July program year; FY 2027-28 notice expected about December 2026. Action Plan due to HUD by mid-August.)
- Layering notes: City is its own HUD entitlement and is outside the Riverside Urban County CDBG/HOME pool in the county record. HOME is small (under $1M a year), so it functions as a slice of the local gap. Federal Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units. The draft Action Plan says the City dedicates its direct PLHA allocation to affordable housing development as additional leverage.

- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**City of Riverside Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) direct formula allocation, development loans**
- Agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Five-year PLHA plan (adopted July 7, 2020) estimated $9,732,750. CY 2023 application $2,456,509 (March 2025). Development loans to date: $1,000,000 Golden Pierce (79 units), $1,053,907 The Aspire (32 youth PSH units), $380,562 Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units), $250,000 proposed for Grapevine (10 units). A large share also goes to homeless case management ($1,384,134 City Net).
- AMI requirement: PLHA rules: rental units at or below 60% AMI (up to 120% AMI for owner units), 55-year covenants.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Awarded through Council-approved loan agreements; uncommitted amounts may be transferred to the Local Affordable Housing Trust Fund ($1.5M already moved). Contact Housing and Human Services.)
- Layering notes: City receives its own PLHA formula share separate from the County PLHA record, so City projects can carry both a City and a County PLHA loan. Commonly stacked with City HOME and PIP on the same project (Sunrise at Bogart used PIP $1.44M, PLHA $380K and HOME $1.51M).
- Source: https://riversideca.legistar1.com/riversideca/attachments/0e2435f5-b0f3-4816-8f98-68582b8bd16d.pdf

**Housing Authority and Successor Agency land write-downs and surplus land dispositions (e.g., 2882 Mission Inn Avenue DDA, 11049 Bogart, 8733 Indiana)**
- Agency: Housing Authority of the City of Riverside; Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency of the City of Riverside
- Type: land
- Typical award: Land conveyed at or near $1. Example: September 1, 2026 DDA conveys 2882 Mission Inn Ave (0.22 acre) to Grapevine Development for $1, a $245,861 write-down counted as HOME match, for 10 affordable units in a 64-unit mixed-use project; that project also pairs $900,000 City HOME and $250,000 City PLHA with LIHTC. Other Housing Authority sites: 11049 Bogart (DDA with NPHS, 22 PSH units), 8733 Indiana (RFP with adjacent Successor Agency parcel), 2348 University (duplex redevelopment).
- AMI requirement: Surplus Land Act: at least 25% lower income on the notice of availability, 55-year covenants; Grapevine DDA requires 2 units at 50% AMI and 8 at 60% AMI for 55 years.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Sites are offered through SLA notices and RFPs as they come up; watch Housing Authority agendas. The University Avenue Density Transfer Pilot (separate record) also targets City surplus parcels.)
- Layering notes: Land write-downs count as HOME match (City reports excess HOME match of $16.4M). Successor Agency parcels need Countywide Oversight Board approval and HCD SLA sign-off, which adds months. The County land program (county record) is separate.
- Source: https://riversideca.legistar1.com/riversideca/attachments/b93e9147-b9ff-49dd-836f-73b65f7a2d6f.docx

**Housing Authority of the City of Riverside, Housing Successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF)**
- Agency: Housing Authority of the City of Riverside (Housing Successor to the former Redevelopment Agency)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: FY 2023-24 (latest report found, dated April 1, 2025): $9,403,323 deposited, $2,899,271 spent ($1,597,196 on housing development across ELI, VLI and low income units), ending cash balance $2,547,069. Portfolio $35.6M ($34.9M loans receivable, $685K real property). The Housing Authority also owns 104 units managed by RHDC under a 2024 operating agreement.
- AMI requirement: LMIHAF rules (HSC 34176.1): at least 30% of spending for ELI (30% AMI) and no more than 20% for 60 to 80% AMI over each five-year period; 55-year rental covenants typical.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No standing NOFA. Funds and Housing Authority land are committed project by project through Council and Housing Authority actions; contact Housing and Human Services.)
- Layering notes: Separate from the County housing successor (HACR) record; only for projects inside city limits. Used alongside City HOME/PLHA and land write-downs (see Housing Authority land record). Ending balance is modest, so treat as a supplemental source. A FY 2024-25 report was not found on the City site (404) and should be requested.
- Source: https://riversideca.gov/hhs/sites/riversideca.gov.hhs/files/Housing%20Successor%20LMIHF%20FY%202023-24.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Prohousing designation and Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) loans, City of Riverside**
- Agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department (designation by HCD)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: City has received $2.44M in PIP to date: $1,000,000 loan to Mulberry Gardens Family (149 units) and $1,440,000 to Sunrise at Bogart (22 PSH units). Council authorized an application for up to $1,440,000 in PIP Round 4 (March 24, 2026); loans come back to Council project by project.
- AMI requirement: PIP-assisted units at or below 50% AMI; 55-year covenants in first position.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Prohousing designation (awarded March 30, 2023) expires January 1, 2027. The Housing and Homelessness Committee took up reapplication on August 31, 2026; a reapplication resolution and HCD submittal must happen before January 2027 for the City to keep PIP eligibility and Prohousing scoring points.)
- Layering notes: Designation also gives Riverside projects Prohousing points or preference in HCD competitive programs (AHSC, IIG and others), a meaningful edge for City sites. PIP residual receipts flow to the LAHTF. Risk: staff estimate 16 confident and up to 23 uncertain points against a 30-point threshold under the stricter 2024 criteria, so the designation could lapse. Recorded at city level because the City selects and lends to projects, although the money is HCD's.
- Source: https://riversideca.legistar1.com/riversideca/attachments/6a5bf8ac-0390-4374-8266-cbdc5145ea9a.docx
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Riverside Local Affordable Housing Trust Fund (LAHTF), created by Council resolution March 12, 2024**
- Agency: City of Riverside Housing and Human Services Department
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Construction and permanent loans at simple interest of no more than 3% per annum, with repayments recycled into the fund. Seeded with a $1,500,000 transfer of PLHA funds; ongoing revenue from HOME, NSP, CalHome, PLHA and ARPA affordable housing program income (ARPA affordable housing allocation was $1,388,797) plus 50% of future sale proceeds of City-owned land bought with General Fund money. City applied for a $1,000,000 HCD Local Housing Trust Fund match (August 2024). Staff cite typical gap requests of $3M to $4M for 65 to 80 unit projects.
- AMI requirement: Low to moderate income households. Committee recommendations at creation: 99-year affordability term, priority for seniors and justice-involved people, and eligibility for market-rate developers that restrict 10% of rental units (or 5% of for-sale units). Loans funded with PIP Round 4 money require 55-year first-position covenants at or below 50% AMI.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No LAHTF NOFA issued as of 2026-11-08. The March 24, 2026 PIP Round 4 staff report says residual receipts from PIP loans will flow to the trust fund and staff will issue a NOFA once enough has accumulated. Contact Housing and Human Services (Agripina Neubauer, Housing Project Manager).)
- Layering notes: City-controlled gap layer that sits ahead of County HOME/PLHA (the County CDBG/HOME record covers the Urban County, which excludes the City of Riverside as its own entitlement grantee). Stacks with the City's own HOME, PLHA and PIP loans (separate records) and with 4% or 9% LIHTC. Capitalized mainly from recycled program income, so the balance is small relative to need; expect it to be combined with HOME and PLHA on the same project. If the LHTF state match was awarded it carries HCD LHTF regulatory terms. City pages on riversideca.gov are thin; staff reports were pulled through the Legistar web API (client riversideca).
- Source: https://riversideca.legistar1.com/riversideca/attachments/1ba55bf5-5dbd-4eeb-9ca6-933968bf57e8.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Riverside density bonus, Municipal Code Chapter 19.545**
- Agency: City of Riverside Community and Economic Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Implements state density bonus law with a concession table (1 to 4 concessions; 100% affordable projects get 4 and, within half a mile of a major transit stop, up to three extra stories or 33 feet) and reduced parking ratios (1 space for 0-1 BR, 1.5 for 2-3 BR; 0.5 per unit near transit with at least 11% VLI or 20% low).
- AMI requirement: Eligibility per Gov. Code 65915: 5% VLI, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 10% special populations, 20% lower income students, or 100% lower income with up to 20% moderate.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applied through entitlement review. Zoning Code amendments (PR-2024-001746 and the 2025 omnibus PR-2025-001793) updated Chapter 19.545 for 2024 state law changes.)
- Layering notes: No local enhancements beyond state law found; the chapter tracks Gov. Code 65915. City has no inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee fund, and no adopted citywide affordable housing fee deferral program was found. Pairs with the University Avenue Density Transfer Pilot (separate record) on eligible sites.
- Source: https://riversideca.legistar1.com/riversideca/attachments/7d869dac-66e3-4bb9-9bc2-642278a8e580.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**University Avenue Density Transfer Pilot Program (Housing Element Program HE-EJ-7-2)**
- Agency: City of Riverside Community and Economic Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: zoning incentive
- Typical award: Not a cash subsidy. Creates a unit bank seeded with residential capacity from City-owned surplus parcels in the University Avenue Specific Plan; receiver sites (City surplus and Housing Element sites) can withdraw extra units first-come first-served, with priority to City surplus sites, and may combine withdrawals with Chapter 19.545 density bonuses.
- AMI requirement: None specific to the transfer; affordability comes from density bonus, SLA covenants or funding sources used on the receiver site.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Land Use Committee recommended approval; the Council item (Legistar 52587, March 2026) showed status Agenda Ready with no recorded vote in the API. Verify adoption with Planning before relying on it.)
- Layering notes: Most useful when paired with a City surplus parcel disposition (see land write-down record). Pilot limited to the University Avenue Specific Plan area; may expand if successful.

### City of Rocklin

**Rocklin Affordable Housing Incentive Program (AHIP): Low/Mod Housing Fund residual receipts loans (Resolution 2024-039, repealed and replaced September 9, 2025)**
- Agency: City of Rocklin City Manager's Office, Housing Division (Housing@rocklin.ca.us; 3970 Rocklin Road, 916-625-5000)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Residual receipts loan of up to $40,000 for each very low and extremely low income unit constructed, funded from the City's Low/Mod Housing Fund. Approved subsidies as of September 2025 (contingent on full project financing): CHW Pacific Street Apartments, 109 affordable units, $2.6 million; USA Properties The Steven, 179 affordable age-restricted units, $2.23 million. AHIP was adopted January 23, 2024 and restated September 9, 2025 to align its fee deferral component with SB 937; the loan and fee reduction terms were unchanged.
- AMI requirement: Loans attach to units restricted to very low (50% AMI) and extremely low (30% AMI) income households; the fee reduction companion applies at 60% AMI or lower; qualified affordable housing developments per the AHIP resolution.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No NOFA; developers request a commitment from the Housing Division during entitlement so the City estimate can be included in LIHTC applications. Confirm the remaining Low/Mod Housing Fund balance with staff; the two approved commitments total $4.83 million.)
- Layering notes: Rocklin's only direct gap source; it stacks with the 40% impact fee reduction and SB 937 fee deferral (next record), the new inclusionary in-lieu fee trust fund, Placer County in-lieu fee loans and Housing Trust Placer, and PBVs from either Roseville Housing Authority or Placer County Housing Authority (both cover Rocklin). Rocklin is in the Roseville, Rocklin and Placer County Continuum of Care (CA-515). The City's websites (rocklin.ca.us legacy and rocklin.ca.gov CivicPlus) return 403 to scripts; staff reports were read from the City's Legistar packet files on d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net and the fee deferral form from the DocumentCenter.
- Source: https://d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net/rocklin-ca/0ec9880a92fca65f4afaea2f351002320.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rocklin Density Increase Incentive Program (Municipal Code Chapter 17.96, Ordinance 977) and Housing Element Program 10 Residential Minimum Density Overlay rezones (August 26, 2025)**
- Agency: City of Rocklin Community Development Department, Planning Division (Arwen Wacht, Planning Manager; Nathan Anderson, Principal Planner)
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory incentive, not a subsidy. Chapter 17.96 (2011) incorporates Government Code 65915 by reference for projects of five or more units in any residential zone: bonus amounts and concessions as specified in state law, applications processed with entitlements and approved if state criteria are met, affordability secured for 30 years or longer if required by financing. Separately, on August 26, 2025 Council approved General Plan amendments, a CEQA addendum and an ordinance applying the Residential Minimum Density Overlay (Chapter 17.53) to alternative RHNA sites to cure the shortfall HCD identified in its April 8, 2025 letter, including sites in the Rocklin West annexation.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus thresholds; 30-year minimum affordability covenant in the local chapter (state law now requires 55 years for rental units, which controls).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Processed with entitlements. Confirm the final adoption date of the alternative sites rezone ordinance (introduced August 26, 2025) and the current RHNA site list with Planning.)
- Layering notes: No local enhancements beyond state law; Rocklin's incentives sit in AHIP (fee reduction, Low/Mod loans) rather than the density bonus chapter. The minimum density overlay sites are the practical pipeline of by-right multifamily land for 2021 to 2029 RHNA units. Chapter text read on the zoneomics mirror; the August 26, 2025 staff report cover was read from the Legistar packet on d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net.

- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rocklin Inclusionary Housing Requirements (Municipal Code Chapter 17.95, Ordinance 1195, November 11, 2025) and in-lieu fee into the Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund**
- Agency: City of Rocklin Community Development Department, Planning Division, with the City Manager's Office Housing Division
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Housing development projects of 10 or more units must provide 15% of units for low income households, or 10% for very low income, or 5% for extremely low income (rental projects provide rental units; fractional units round up). Exempt: projects complete or with SB 330 preliminary applications before the effective date, projects with at least 50% affordable units, historic landmark portions and statutory development agreement projects. Alternatives: off-site construction, acquisition and rehabilitation of market-rate units, or an in-lieu fee once set by Council resolution, paid before building permit into a separate Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund. Council held a January 13, 2026 hearing on a proposed interim fee of $10 per square foot (opposed by the California Apartment Association) and, per the City's June 9, 2026 Council recap found in search results but not opened, approved an in-lieu fee of $2.75 per square foot with further ordinance updates still in progress. Paying the fee does not qualify a project for a state density bonus.
- AMI requirement: Rental inclusionary units restricted 55 years, for-sale units 45 years, by recorded inclusionary housing agreement approved by Council with the entitlements; units dispersed and comparable to market-rate units; the City tenant preference policy applies.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies to applications deemed complete after the ordinance took effect (December 2025). The $2.75 per square foot fee and the trust fund guidelines should be confirmed with Planning; a broader fee study (consultant RFP issued 2024) and ordinance amendments were pending in mid-2026.)
- Layering notes: New in 2025, so the Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund has little or no balance yet; over time it will feed the AHIP Low/Mod loans. A 100% affordable project is exempt and instead benefits from the ordinance by competing for the fee revenue. Compare Placer County Chapter 15.65 (10% inclusionary, unincorporated area). The ordinance text was verified on the zoneomics mirror of the Rocklin code; the fee resolution and June 9, 2026 staff report could not be opened (rocklin.ca.gov 403, Legistar API returns 500 for client rocklin), hence needs_confirmation.
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/rocklin-CA/chapter_65
- Confidence: needs_confirmation (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rocklin impact fee reduction of 40% for affordable units (Ordinance 1159, January 10, 2023) and SB 937 fee deferral program (Resolution adopted August 26, 2025)**
- Agency: City of Rocklin City Manager's Office, Housing Division (Housing@rocklin.ca.us) and Community Development Department
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: 40% reduction of City development impact fees for deed-restricted units at 60% AMI or lower, calculated unit by unit (adopted by Ordinance 1159 with the rate set by resolution the same night). Fee deferral: City park development, traffic, community and recreation center, construction tax, park improvement, public facilities and trails impact fees deferred from building permit to final inspection or certificate of occupancy, secured by a promissory note and deed of trust that may be subordinated to construction financing; since the August 26, 2025 SB 937 policy, deferral to final inspection applies to all designated residential projects without interest, and the AHIP deferral is aligned with it. Staff reported in September 2025 that no reductions or deferrals had yet been processed but estimates had been issued to developers for their financing packages.
- AMI requirement: Fee reduction: units deed-restricted at 60% AMI or lower. AHIP fee deferral eligibility: at least 10% of units at affordable rents for very low income households or at least 49% of units affordable to low income households; fees become payable with interest penalties if the promised units are not delivered by certificate of occupancy.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Apply to Housing@rocklin.ca.us with a preliminary title report before building permit issuance; reductions must be requested before signing a deferral agreement. Municipal Code chapters on impact fees were slated for SB 937 clean-up at a future Council meeting (not confirmed adopted as of this pass).)
- Layering notes: A real cost reduction (not just timing), unlike Roseville, which defers but does not waive. Combine with the $40,000 per unit Low/Mod loan (record above). Placer County Capital Facilities fees and school fees are outside the City program. Verified from the September 9, 2025 Council staff report and the City's fee deferral application form (rocklin.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/457).
- Source: https://www.rocklin.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/457
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of Rohnert Park

**Rohnert Park Affordable Housing Linkage Fee (Municipal Code Chapter 3.36)**
- Agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Nonresidential projects (new buildings, added square footage, remodels or changes of use that increase employment density) pay a linkage fee based on classification: commercial $0.69, retail $1.19 and industrial $0.71 per square foot, rates effective July 1, 2008 and apparently never updated (Development Impact Fees handout revised July 16, 2026). Fund 4225 (Affordable Linkage Fee) held $13,430 at June 30, 2023 after $285,000 of expenditures.
- AMI requirement: Proceeds support affordable housing for very low, low and moderate income households under the inclusionary ordinance's use-of-fees rules.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fee in effect at building permit; no scheduled update found. A 2024 Generation Housing action plan recommended impact fee reform in Rohnert Park; no council action confirmed.)
- Layering notes: Revenue is minor compared with the Rental Affordable Housing Fee and in-lieu fee, so it adds little gap capacity; it is listed for completeness. Petaluma and Santa Rosa linkage fees are several times higher. Read from the City's Development Impact Fees handout (rpcity.ca.gov DocumentCenter); the Chapter 3.36 code text was not opened (municipal code hosts block scripts).
- Source: https://www.rpcity.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/188/Development-Fees-Handout-PDF
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rohnert Park Density Bonus (Municipal Code Section 17.08.020) and affordable housing concessions under Section 17.08.010(E)**
- Agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory. Section 17.08.020 adopts state density bonus law (Government Code 65915 et seq.) by reference with no local increase beyond the state schedule; it sets application contents (project summary table, base and bonus unit counts, replacement housing compliance, parking) and ministerial processing without separate Planning Commission action. Section 17.08.010(E) lets the City Council grant for-sale projects exceeding the inclusionary requirement, and rental projects that include affordable units, additional concessions: an extra density bonus or incentives of equal financial value, waiver of City standards, direct financial assistance (loan or grant) from trust funds, and deferral of all City fees on market-rate units until certificate of occupancy. Projects making all inclusionary units affordable at median, low or very low income get an additional 5% density bonus.
- AMI requirement: State thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable) for the state bonus; Council discretion for the local concessions, tied to on-site affordable units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Submitted with the entitlement application; Council concessions requested through the project approval or a development agreement. Housing Element Program HO-3.B (City Density Bonus Program) and HO-2.E (Workforce Housing Overlay, to be presented by January 2026 and adopted by December 2026 if directed) may add local bonuses; status not confirmed.)
- Layering notes: Rohnert Park relies on development agreements and specific plans rather than a formal local bonus, so negotiate fee deferral, rental fee relief and gap funding together. The Workforce Housing Overlay would be the first local density tool beyond state law; check Planning for its status. The County's density bonus chapter applies only in unincorporated areas. Read from the zoneomics mirror of Title 17 (Ordinance 991, January 27, 2026 version).
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/rohnert-park-CA/chapter_6
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rohnert Park Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, Municipal Code Section 17.08.010 (re-adopted by Ordinance 991, January 27, 2026): for-sale inclusionary units, Housing In-Lieu Fee and Rental Affordable Housing Fee**
- Agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department (Planning and Building)
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. For-sale projects over 50 units: 15% of units affordable, half low income (80% AMI) and half moderate income (120% AMI), with 99-year resale restrictions; for-sale projects of 50 units or fewer may instead pay the Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee of $15,891.95 per unit (Development Impact Fees handout revised July 16, 2026). All new rental projects pay the Rental Affordable Housing Fee of $4.11 per square foot at building permit (first adopted at $3.23 per square foot; adjusted each July 1 by the ENR-CCI San Francisco index); market-rate rental projects have no on-site unit requirement since the 2019 amendment. Fee revenue goes to a segregated affordable housing account used for acquisition, construction and rehabilitation of affordable housing, subsidies, and assistance to other entities, with an annual public report. Developers providing all required units at median, low or very low income get an extra 5% density bonus; alternatives (land donation, transferable inclusionary credits, off-site units, second units for up to half the requirement) need Council approval.
- AMI requirement: For-sale inclusionary units: 99-year minimum agreements; rental projects pay the fee instead. Exemptions include projects with vested rights, fire or disaster rebuilds of the same size, and projects whose development agreement sets alternative affordable housing terms.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fees adjust every July 1 (ENR-CCI); planning and building application fees are being restudied for a July 1, 2027 update. Ordinance 991 (comprehensive Title 17 update) was adopted January 27, 2026. Large specific plan areas (University District, Southeast Specific Plan, SOMO Village, Downtown) are governed by development agreements that set their own affordable housing terms (University District and SESP at 15%; downtown CenterCal project exempted from the rental fee in exchange for pursuing 15 affordable units).)
- Layering notes: The Rental Affordable Housing Fee is Rohnert Park's main local housing revenue source since the 2011 loss of redevelopment; proceeds (budget Fund 4220) plus in-lieu fees fund gap assistance negotiated case by case (see Rohnert Park affordable housing funds record). A 100% affordable rental project would owe the $4.11 per square foot fee unless waived through a development agreement or the Section 17.08.010(I) adjustment process, so request a waiver early. Rohnert Park's for-sale requirement is lower than City of Sonoma's 25% and Petaluma's 15% (which also covers rentals). Ordinance text read from the zoneomics mirror of Title 17; fee amounts from the City's Development Impact Fees handout on rpcity.ca.gov (the former rpcity.org pages redirect and return 404).
- Source: https://www.rpcity.ca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/188/Development-Fees-Handout-PDF
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Rohnert Park affordable housing funds (Rental Affordable Housing Fee and Housing In-Lieu Fee account, Housing Fund) and Essential Housing Bond Financing Program (Housing Element Programs HO-3.F and bond program)**
- Agency: City of Rohnert Park Development Services Department and City Manager's office; City Council approves assistance
- Type: loan
- Typical award: No NOFA; the City provides gap loans or grants and land through development agreements and Council action, drawing on the segregated affordable housing fee account (budget Funds 4220 Affordable Housing Rental Fee and 4225 Affordable Linkage Fee) and the Housing Fund named in the 2023-2031 Housing Element as a funding source for Programs HO-1.B and HO-3.F (affordable housing on underutilized City sites, including extremely low income units). The Housing Element's Essential Housing Bond Financing Program commits the City to authorize CSCDA or another JPA to issue an estimated $191.3 million in governmental-purpose bonds for acquisition-conversion of market-rate apartments and new deed-restricted housing, forgoing about $337,346 in property tax and targeting at least 222 units (99 very low, 57 low, 66 moderate). Current fund balances and any adopted lending guidelines were not found; the City's budget and Housing Successor (LMIHAF) reports could not be located online.
- AMI requirement: Fee revenue must serve very low, low and moderate income households (Section 17.08.010(J)); bond program units for very low to moderate income; City-site projects target extremely low income units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No open round as of November 10, 2026. No NOFA; assistance is negotiated through development agreements and Council action. Contact Development Services (707-588-2231, Planning@rpcity.org).)
- Layering notes: Rohnert Park was Prohousing designated August 4, 2023 (42 points), which gives projects in the city AHSC and IIG scoring preferences. Local money is thin, so the practical stack is County CFH, County PLHA (Rohnert Park is a non-entitlement city within the County PLHA), RED Housing Fund and County PBVs (county records) plus LIHTC, with the City contributing fee deferrals, land (Program HO-3.F) or a modest gap loan. Rohnert Park's former Community Development Commission was a redevelopment agency, so a Housing Successor LMIHAF may exist; no annual report was found (flag for follow-up). The CivicPlus agenda search on rpcity.ca.gov returned no results for affordable housing and the old rpcity.org pages 404, so recent council actions could not be verified. Source is the adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element on the City's DocumentCenter.

### City of Roseville

**City-owned land for affordable housing: 505 Royer Street and 300 Taylor Street sale to Eden Housing (Resolution 26-331, September 16, 2026)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Economic Development Department (Gina McColl, 916-774-5452) with the Housing Division
- Type: land
- Typical award: Land sale at appraised value rather than a grant: two parcels totaling 1.17 acres in the Downtown Specific Plan (former Placer County courthouse site, demolished 2021, declared surplus October 23, 2019) sold to Eden Housing for $580,000 after a May 2025 RFP (Eden was the sole respondent) for a 58-unit senior affordable project at 30% to 60% AMI. Eden's RFP proposal is a 58-unit senior project at 30% to 60% AMI; deeper restrictions will come from the project's financing regulatory agreements.

**Roseville 10% Affordable Housing Goal in Specific Plan Areas (General Plan Policy LU5.5, Housing Element Programs 6 and 9) with Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreements and case-by-case in-lieu fees**
- Agency: City of Roseville Housing Division (compliance) and Development Services Department, Planning Division (specific plans)
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Every specific plan area must designate 10% of total units as affordable (General Plan goal since 1989: 20% of the affordable units at middle income up to 100% AMI, 40% low income up to 80% AMI, 40% very low income up to 50% AMI), allocated to specific medium and high density parcels and secured by Development Agreements and Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreements recorded before building permits or final small-lot maps. Since 1989 the policy has produced 5,167 affordable units (1,357 very low rental, 2,271 low rental, 427 middle rental, 325 moderate rental, plus 787 purchase units), about 140 per year. The City has no formal in-lieu fee ordinance; in-lieu fees are negotiated case by case ($1,036,410 collected 2013 to 2021). A 2025 Housing Tools Inclusionary Housing Policy Analysis recommended standard fee levels, for example $150,000 per required affordable for-sale unit in projects under 20 units, applied in the East Street Subdivision amendment approved November 4, 2026.
- AMI requirement: Rental units restricted by Affordable Rental Housing Agreements (about 2,700 units under agreement in the 2021 to 2029 period); density bonus (Chapter 19.28) may be assigned by the Regulatory Agreement as part of the subsidy. Sierra Vista Specific Plan: 10% of 8,679 units (about 868) allocated to MDR and HDR parcels, with transfers and credits between parcels allowed by Housing Division approval.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at specific plan and Development Agreement approval; the in-lieu fee option is considered case by case at agreement amendment. The 2021 Housing Element also directs work on a commercial linkage fee (nexus study November 2021, draft ordinance posted, not adopted as of this pass).)
- Layering notes: The reason Roseville has a steady supply of affordable parcels and developers: specific plan landowners (Sierra Vista, West Roseville, Amoruso Ranch, Villages West and others) carry a 10% obligation and typically deliver dedicated HDR parcels or partner with USA Properties, Mercy Housing, St. Anton, Eden Housing and others. Hope Way and the County in-lieu fee program (County Code Chapter 15.65) apply only in unincorporated Placer; inside Roseville this goal and the Regulatory Agreements govern. In-lieu fees collected flow to the Local Housing Trust Fund (record above). Density bonus units are excluded from the 10% base. Verified from the adopted 2021 Housing Element PDF, the Sierra Vista Specific Plan Affordable Housing chapter and the November 4, 2026 Council packet.
- Source: https://www.roseville.ca.gov/Documents/Development%20Services/Planning/Housing%20Element/Housing%20Element.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Roseville CDBG entitlement and HOME funds (annual Action Plan) and Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Plan adopted September 2, 2026**
- Agency: City of Roseville Housing Division (Dani Calli, Housing Analyst, 916-774-5277, dcalli@roseville.ca.gov)
- Type: grant
- Typical award: Roseville is a HUD entitlement city; the 2026-27 CDBG award was expected at roughly $700,000 with about $730,000 of prior-year carryover and about $50,000 program income (2026 Action Plan hearing May 6, 2026; 2025-26 CAPER public comment August 29 to September 16, 2026). CDBG is mostly used for owner rehabilitation loans (deferred loans up to $100,000, $5,000 grants for elderly and disabled owners), accessibility work (over $1 million earmarked in 2026 for Sierra Gardens accessibility upgrades) and public services, but it has funded affordable housing land acquisition: a $571,850 CDBG loan to Greek Orthodox Housing Corporation on September 4, 2024 for parcel JM-30 (192-unit Sierra Vista Apartments). HOME funds (state-administered) support first-time homebuyer and rehabilitation programs. PLHA: Roseville's formula allocation under HCD's July 2026 NOFA (about $285 million statewide, five-year term) is programmed in the City's PLHA Plan (Resolution 26-327) for Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing, not development; $1,374,763 of PLHA was budgeted for HPRR in FY2026-27.
- AMI requirement: CDBG national objective (low and moderate income benefit; 2026 Sacramento PMSA limits: 1 person $73,600, 4 persons $105,100); HOME and PLHA income rules per program.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The 2026 round closed February 2, 2026 and the Action Plan was heard May 6, 2026. No 2027-28 CDBG or HPRR NOFA was posted on the City CDBG page; past cycles released the NOFA in October to January with applications due in late January or early February, so expect a deadline around early February 2027.)
- Layering notes: Roseville runs its own CDBG and PLHA; Placer County's PLHA allocation (county record, needs_confirmation) covers the unincorporated area and non-entitlement cities such as Auburn, while Lincoln became its own CDBG entitlement in 2026 and Rocklin receives its own PLHA formula share. CDBG land loans trigger federal cross-cutting rules (Davis-Bacon for 8 or more units, environmental review, Section 3). PLHA is currently committed to HPRR, so do not count on PLHA for development in Roseville. The CDBG page, PLHA notice and the September 2, 2026 agenda were opened; the PLHA Plan PDF link itself was not fetched.

**Roseville Housing Authority (RHA) Project-Based Vouchers and Housing Choice Vouchers (jurisdiction includes Rocklin)**
- Agency: Roseville Housing Authority, a department of the City of Roseville (Housing Division, 916-774-5270, housing@roseville.ca.gov)
- Type: rental assistance
- Typical award: Rental subsidy, not capital. RHA (established October 2, 1974) administers tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers for roughly 850 households (about 1,600 individuals) at or below 50% AMI in Roseville and Rocklin, plus VASH and Mainstream vouchers. It project-bases vouchers in new affordable developments (the City's news release on The Crawford, 265 units by USA Properties, cites eight RHA project-based vouchers) and runs a Project Based Voucher waiting list (waitlistcheck.com CA1217-4334). Payment standards effective October 1, 2026 and utility allowances effective June 1, 2026 are posted for Roseville (95661, 95678, 95747) and Rocklin.
- AMI requirement: HCV income limits: 50% AMI at admission (2026: 1 person $46,000, 4 persons $65,700), with 75% of new admissions at or below 30% AMI; PBV units must meet HUD HQS and the Housing Element directs RHA to expand use in high opportunity areas.
- Cycle: rolling (next: PBV commitments are requested from RHA during predevelopment; RHA reports quarterly to Council (next quarterly status update early 2027). Contact RHA before TCAC or CDLAC applications to secure a PBV commitment letter.)
- Layering notes: Roseville and Rocklin projects have two voucher sources: RHA (city) and Placer County Housing Authority (county record, PBVs and special-purpose vouchers); Rocklin is covered by both. PBVs raise achievable rents on 30% AMI units and support bond or 4% deals. Not a public works trigger by itself. Verified on the RHA page opened this pass.
- Source: https://www.roseville.ca.gov/departments/affordable_housing/housing_authority/index.php
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Roseville Housing Successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (SB 341 reports; Housing Element Program 12)**
- Agency: City of Roseville acting as Housing Successor to the former Redevelopment Agency; Housing Division
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Small gap loans and Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing grants. Fund balance $2,379,350 at June 30, 2025 (FY2024-25 deposits $1,032,069, including $737,249 from the 20% share of City loan payoffs; FY2024-25 expenditures $434,196 with $0 for development). Past development loans: $5,760,000 to Mercy Housing for 623 Vernon Street (58 units, 2016 to 2018), $600,000 deferred loan to Junction Crossing (80 units, approved October 20, 2021), $500,000 to Hampstead's Prospera at Fiddyment workforce housing (104 units, approved April 3, 2024). HPRR spending is capped at $250,000 per year; on September 2, 2026 Council budgeted $1,250,000 from the fund for FY2026-27 together with $1,374,763 of PLHA.
- AMI requirement: Health and Safety Code 34176.1 targeting: development money must serve households at or below 80% AMI, with at least 30% spent on 30% AMI households and no more than 20% on 60% to 80% AMI; 55-year covenants used; no senior-only restriction issue (0% of assisted units senior-restricted in the last 10 years).
- Cycle: rolling (next: No NOFA; developers approach the Housing Division. Revenue is only loan repayments (projected through 2036), so expect commitments of a few hundred thousand dollars per project. The FY2025-26 SB 341 report is due by December 31, 2026.)
- Layering notes: Roseville is the only Placer jurisdiction with a Housing Successor fund actively lending (Lincoln has a Redevelopment Successor Agency but no housing fund activity was found; Rocklin's Low/Mod Housing Fund is described under its Affordable Housing Incentive Program). Stacks with LHTF and PIP money (record above), PLHA, county in-lieu fee loans and LIHTC. Excess surplus test: the balance must stay under the greater of $1,000,000 or four years of deposits, which pushes the City to commit funds. Read from the FY2024-25 SB 341 Report of Required Information posted on the Affordable Housing Funds page.

**Roseville Local Housing Trust Fund (LHTF) gap loans, including Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) program income NOFA (Resolution 26-404, November 4, 2026)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Economic Development Department, Housing Division (316 Vernon Street, Suite 150; 916-774-5270; housing@roseville.ca.gov)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Project-by-project gap loans from the City's Local Housing Trust Fund, which receives in-lieu fees, affordable purchase loan payoffs and state grant program income. Most recent round: a NOFA released August 31, 2026 offered $1,000,000 of PIP program income (from a $1,050,000 developer loan payoff on the City's 2023 PIP Round 1 award of $1,610,000) for predevelopment of lower-income rental housing; two applications were received (Eden Housing, 505 Royer, 58 senior units; Mercy Housing, Pleasant Grove Apartments Phase II, 49 units) and staff recommended reserving the full $1,000,000 for Pleasant Grove Phase II on November 4, 2026. Earlier LHTF and in-lieu commitments include $4.36M reserved for Junction Crossing (80 units, St. Anton) and, per the City's pipeline report, $6,000,000 for Pleasant Grove Apartments (pipeline PDF returned 502 this pass). The 2021 Housing Element commits the City to re-apply for state LHTF matching funds as rounds open.
- AMI requirement: Set by loan documents and an Affordable Rental Housing Agreement; PIP money is limited to lower-income (at or below 80% AMI) rental housing, and the 2026 NOFA targeted 30% to 60% AMI projects with preference for units for persons with disabilities and supportive services. Projects in high opportunity areas or areas at risk of displacement are prioritized (Housing Element Programs 9, 10 and 12).
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: No open round as of November 8, 2026; the August 31, 2026 PIP program-income NOFA closed and $1,000,000 was reserved for Pleasant Grove Apartments Phase II on November 4, 2026. Loan documents return to Council at a future meeting. Watch for the next LHTF or PIP program-income NOFA from the Housing Division.)
- Layering notes: This is the city layer that stacks under 9% or 4% LIHTC and tax-exempt bonds (county TEFRA via CalPFA, CMFA or CSCDA; the County is not an issuer). Roseville's LHTF is separate from Placer County's in-lieu fee gap loans (Hope Way, Destination at Placer One) and from Housing Trust Placer; a Roseville project can seek all three plus Roseville Housing Authority project-based vouchers. Gap order: LIHTC and bonds first, then City LHTF or PIP reservation, then County or Housing Trust Placer money. Roseville's municipal website (roseville.ca.us, now roseville.ca.gov) opens, but the pipeline PDF and script-rendered agenda pages do not; staff reports were read from the City's CivicClerk API file streams (rosevilleca.api.civicclerk.com).

**Roseville Residential Density Bonus (Zoning Ordinance Chapter 19.28) and Prohousing Designation renewal (Resolution 25-346, November 5, 2025)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Development Services Department, Planning Division (Lauren Hocker, Senior Planner, 916-774-5272)
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory incentive, not a subsidy. Chapter 19.28 mirrors Government Code 65915: bonuses of 20% to 50% for very low, lower and moderate income set-asides, 80% (or no limit near major transit) for 100% affordable projects, 20% for senior, foster youth, disabled veteran and homeless housing, 35% for student housing, land donation and child care bonuses, up to four incentives, parking caps (0.5 space per unit for qualifying projects near transit, none for 100% lower-income rental near transit or qualifying senior projects). Applications require a pro forma, an appraisal of the bonus value and a sources and uses statement showing the financing gap. Roseville was among the first ten Prohousing-designated jurisdictions (2022); the designation expired at the end of 2025 and Council authorized renewal on November 5, 2025 (application published for 30-day review through September 29, 2025). The City reports over $1 million in grants attributable to the designation and received $1,610,000 of PIP Round 1 funds in 2023.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, or 100% affordable); Affordable Housing Agreement recorded for 55 years (rental) under Section 19.28.110.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Processed with entitlements; no deadline. HCD action on the Prohousing renewal application was pending at the time of the November 2025 hearing; confirm current designation status with Planning before claiming Prohousing points in MHP, AHSC or IIG applications.)
- Layering notes: No local enhancements beyond state law other than the explicit pro forma and appraisal submittal requirements. Density bonus units do not count toward the 10% specific plan goal, and the Regulatory Agreement can assign bonus units as part of the City's subsidy. Prohousing status gives bonus points on state NOFAs for projects located in Roseville (not available in Rocklin, Lincoln or Auburn, none of which held the designation as of this pass). Chapter text read on the zoneomics code mirror; Roseville's own code host (ecode360) returns partial PDFs only.
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/roseville-CA/chapter_3
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Roseville development impact fee deferral for affordable multifamily (Municipal Code Section 4.04.040, Ordinance 6830; Sierra Vista Apartments deferral, Resolution 26-336)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Economic Development Department (Gina McColl, 916-774-5452) with the Finance Department
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Deferral, not waiver: city-controlled impact fees are deferred from building permit to final or certificate of occupancy, with interest at the City's pooled rate (ten-year average about 2.23%) and an administrative processing fee per permit. Deferrals of $100,000 or more need Council approval. Example approved September 16, 2026: about $2,987,339 deferred for the 192-unit Sierra Vista Apartments (Greek Orthodox Housing Corporation, parcel JM-30, 4950 Upland Drive), covering fire construction tax, sewer and water connection, drainage, SVSP traffic mitigation, citywide and neighborhood parks, bike trail, public benefit and solid waste fees (about $373,000 per building). For a 100% affordable project (three or more units, all units low, very low or extremely low income, Affordable Housing Agreement under Section 19.28.110, objective design standards, secured promissory note) payment may be pushed up to one year after the first certificate of occupancy. The City's policy is not to waive fees; CSCDA SCIP fee financing is also offered.
- AMI requirement: Standard deferral is open to any multifamily project on request; the extended one-year post-occupancy deferral requires 100% of units (except managers) affordable to low, very low or extremely low income households under a recorded Affordable Housing Agreement.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Request through the Economic Development Department when fee estimates are prepared; a Council hearing under Government Code 53083 is required for deferrals of $100,000 or more.)
- Layering notes: Timing relief only; fees are still paid in full with interest, so it does not reduce basis but eases construction-period cash needs. Placer County Capital Facilities fees and traffic fees are not city-controlled and are not deferred; age-restricted projects get reduced traffic and County capital facilities rates. Roseville also made a $571,850 CDBG loan (September 4, 2024) to the same Sierra Vista sponsor for land purchase, showing how CDBG, fee deferral, the Regulatory Agreement and LIHTC stack on one project. Read from the September 16, 2026 City Council agenda packet via the CivicClerk API file stream.
- Source: https://rosevilleca.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=11713,plainText=false)

### City of Sacramento

**City of Sacramento Development Impact Fee Deferral Program**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Building Division (Form CDD-0330)
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Deferral, not waiver: City impact fees may be paid at final inspection instead of permit issuance, useful for phased or multi-building projects. No cost figure published. Fee estimates available for a low-cost application. The Statewide Community Infrastructure Program (CSCDA SCIP) is also accepted for financing eligible City impact fees.
- AMI requirement: None; open to all residential projects.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Apply with CDD-0330 before permit issuance; fees due at final inspection.)
- Layering notes: Carries impact fees through construction so they can be paid from permanent loan proceeds; pair with the Zero-Dollar Rate reduction on the affordable units and SCIP bond financing of remaining fees. The County runs a separate deferral program for unincorporated projects (County record).
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-development-kit/housing-development-incentives/help-me-reduce-the-cost-of-development
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**City of Sacramento Housing Trust Fund (commercial linkage fee, City Code Chapter 18.56 Article IV)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee assessment); SHRA (fund administration and lending)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Fee source for SHRA City gap loans. Nonresidential rates effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: office $3.35, hotel $3.19, commercial $2.69, manufacturing $2.09, warehouse $0.92 per square foot, a 0.49% San Francisco construction cost index adjustment from the FY 2025-26 rates ($3.33, $3.18, $2.68, $2.08, $0.91). Table H in the FY27 notice sets use-specific rates (for example major medical facility $5.22, laboratory $2.84, K-12 and college $2.79). The FY27 notice is attached to the City Fees and Charges database entry (fee ID 3798); the City Housing Trust Fund page still links the FY 2025-26 notice as of 2026-11-10. 2024 fund: $411,805 fees collected, $140,000 spent, $4.85M ending balance of which $807,861 uncommitted; $1.0M posted as available June 1, 2026.
- AMI requirement: Fund is restricted to housing for workforce households up to 80% AMI (very low and low income wage earners) under the 1989 jobs-housing nexus; 55-year SHRA regulatory agreement.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: Deployed through the SHRA two-round schedule. Proposed 2027 SHRA schedule: pre-applications January 4, 2027 and July 1, 2027; full applications March 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027. Fee is paid at building permit on nonresidential projects; contact Ryan Dodge, (916) 808-8044, rdodge@cityofsacramento.org for fee questions.)
- Layering notes: Adopted 1989 (Chapter 17.708), moved into the Development Impact Fee chapter 18.56 on Feb 14, 2017; Council raised the fee 81.3% in 2004 (phased) and allows changes by resolution. Small and lumpy: about $0.4M to $0.6M a year in fees, so it is the smallest of the four City pools and is usually blended into a single SHRA loan with HOME and Mixed Income money. Parallel County Housing Trust Fund covers the unincorporated area (County rates $3.26 office to $1.08 warehouse since March 28, 2025). Annual report posted each May by SHRA.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-trust-fund
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Density bonus (City Code Chapter 17.704) and ministerial infill housing permits (Chapter 17.860 and SB 35/SB 423)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: State density bonus law as implemented in Chapter 17.704 (no local enhancement beyond state minimums identified): e.g., 5% very low income units earns a 20% bonus plus one concession and unlimited waivers; up to 50% bonus and the 100% affordable 80% bonus per Government Code 65915. City ministerial permit (CDD-0428, adopted Aug 27, 2020) covers 2 to 200 unit residential or mixed-use infill projects meeting objective standards, no affordability or prevailing wage requirement, no CEQA, 60 to 90 day review; the state SB 35 permit (CDD-0427) requires 10% lower-income units at 11 or more units. Density bonus requests can be processed ministerially with either permit.
- AMI requirement: Per state law for the bonus; none for the City ministerial permit.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Rolling at entitlement. Parking: none required within a quarter mile of light rail, 50% reduction within a half mile.)
- Layering notes: Sacramento is the state's first Prohousing jurisdiction (renewed Dec 23, 2025 with the top score) and already has high base densities, so the bonus is mostly used for height, parking and setback waivers rather than unit count. Combining the City ministerial permit with a density bonus avoids hearings and CEQA for 100% affordable infill without the SB 35 prevailing wage trigger. Missing Middle zoning (2024) allows multi-unit on former single-family lots citywide.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-development-kit/housing-development-incentives/help-me-build-more-housing-units-or-tailor-my-project-to-my-site
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Mixed Income Housing Ordinance and Housing Impact Fee (City Code Chapter 17.712)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee); SHRA (Mixed Income Housing fund and 100-acre housing strategies)
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement and fee, not a subsidy. Housing Impact Fee effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: $3.58 per square foot for single-unit, duplex and multi-unit dwellings below 20 and 40 dwelling units per net acre respectively; $0.00 for single-unit or duplex at 20 du/acre or more, multi-unit at 40 du/acre or more, and nonresidential-to-residential conversions; $1.55 per square foot in the Housing Incentive Zone. Fee revenue (about $1.7M in 2024, $4.2M lent to projects that year) goes to the SHRA-administered Mixed Income Housing fund; $2.5M posted available June 1, 2026. Projects over 100 gross acres must adopt a Council-approved mixed income housing strategy.
- AMI requirement: Exempt from the fee: developments with 10% regulated low-income units (80% AMI), room additions, second units, owner-builder single homes, mobilehome parks, projects with pre-ordinance development agreements or pre-November 2015 entitlements. No mandatory inclusionary requirement citywide.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fee assessed at building permit, adjusted every July 1. The Housing Element Program H1 review ended Dec 9, 2025 when Council voted to make no changes, so the current structure holds through at least 2027. Contact Greta Soos, (916) 808-2027.)
- Layering notes: Most 4% and 9% multifamily deals in Sacramento pay nothing: at 40 du/acre or more the rate is $0, and any project with 10% low-income units is exempt, so the fee mainly hits single-family subdivisions and low-density apartments. The fund it feeds is the largest City gap pool after HOME ($2.5M June 2026). Compare the County Affordable Housing Ordinance ($3.91 per square foot with on-site credit) for unincorporated sites. A 2023 to 2025 study considered mandatory inclusionary and higher fees; Council declined, so no inclusionary units are required citywide.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-impact-fee
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Multifamily Mortgage Revenue Bonds, Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento (SHRA conduit issuance)**
- Agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency for the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
- Type: bond
- Typical award: Tax-exempt and taxable conduit bonds for rental projects of 12 or more units in the City; no minimum or maximum issue size (cost-effectiveness usually sets a floor). Applications for bonds without an SHRA loan are accepted year round; bond-plus-loan requests follow the SHRA pre-application schedule. Private placements require accredited or qualified institutional buyers in $250,000 denominations with investor letters.
- AMI requirement: Federal minimum 20% at 50% AMI or 30% at 60% AMI plus 10% at 50% AMI (H&S 34312.3); CDLAC and CTCAC rules govern; SHRA adds its 15% at 50% AMI and 5% at 30% AMI policy when an SHRA loan is included; non-competitive CTCAC deals averaging above 60% AMI must average at or below 59% AMI. Refundings that extend maturity require at least 10% of units at 50% or 60% AMI for 15 more years.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Bond-only applications any time; bond-with-loan applications follow the proposed 2027 SHRA schedule: pre-applications January 4, 2027 and July 1, 2027, full applications March 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027, approvals June 29, 2027 and January 25, 2028. SHRA Commission then City Council and Housing Authority approval, then CDLAC allocation.)
- Layering notes: SHRA prefers to be the issuer for City projects and pairs bonds with its gap loan; CSCDA or CMFA remain alternatives if timing does not fit. Bond policy requires the nonprofit owner to have material day-to-day involvement for projects claiming the welfare exemption, matching BOE scrutiny of managing general partners (see County Assessor record). Policies: 2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies (Section 9).
- Source: https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-City-final.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Prohousing Designation (state scoring preference for City of Sacramento projects)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department (designation held by the City; HCD administers the program)
- Type: policy/designation
- Typical award: Not a direct subsidy. Projects in a Prohousing jurisdiction receive priority processing or bonus points in state programs including AHSC, Infill Infrastructure Grant, TCC, TIRCP and related transportation programs, and the City may apply to the Prohousing Incentive Program for added funds. Sacramento was the first designated city (Feb 10, 2022) and renewed Dec 23, 2025 with 108 points, the highest score in the state as of June 2026.
- AMI requirement: None at the project level; benefit flows to any eligible affordable project in the City.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Designation runs on HCD's renewal cycle; next renewal due around 2029. Contact Angel Anguiano, (916) 808-5519.)
- Layering notes: Relevant to layering: AHSC and IIG applications for City sites score Prohousing points that unincorporated-county and most other Sacramento-area cities (Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, Citrus Heights, Folsom were not confirmed as designated this pass) do not get. Check HCD's designated-jurisdictions tracker before assuming points for a non-City site.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/Prohousing
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Reduced Residential Development Impact Fees for Affordable Dwelling Units (Zero-Dollar Rate Program)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (Form CDD-0410); affordability confirmed by SHRA or CADA
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Reduction of City-controlled development impact fees to a $0 rate for deed-restricted affordable units, capped at $10,000 per qualifying unit, funded by a $3 million annual General Fund/Measure U appropriation (reauthorized July 2025). Eligible fees: park development impact fee (Ch. 18.56 Art. II), sewer, combined sewer, water system and storm drainage development fees (Ch. 13), and the 65th Street, Central City, Jacinto Creek, North Natomas, Railyards, River District and Willowcreek area fees. School fees and SAFCA fees are not City-controlled and still apply.
- AMI requirement: Rental: occupied by low or moderate income households (80% or 120% AMI per H&S 50093) at affordable rent (H&S 50053), restricted at least 30 years by a recorded regulatory agreement with the City, SHRA or another public agency. For-sale: low income (80% AMI) at an affordable price, 30 years.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Rolling, first come first served against each fiscal year's $3 million allocation; no application deadline. Apply with Form CDD-0410 before permit issuance.)
- Layering notes: Worth roughly $5,000 to $10,000 per unit depending on area fees; stackable with the SacSewer impact fee waiver (County record) which covers the regional sanitation fee the City program does not touch, and with the Housing Impact Fee $0 rate. Because Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats waived fees as public funds, a fee reduction can by itself trigger state prevailing wage for a project that is otherwise exempt; most LIHTC projects already pay prevailing wage. The 2018 version waived fees without a cap; the 2024 modification added the $10,000 cap and the $3M budget, so large projects should not assume full waivers. Deferral of remaining impact fees to final inspection is available separately (CDD-0330).
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/reduction-of-development-impact-fees-for-new-adus
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**SHRA Multifamily Lending Program (City of Sacramento gap financing: HOME, Housing Trust Fund, Mixed Income Housing fund, PLHA)**
- Agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (SHRA) on behalf of the City of Sacramento and the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Gap loans sized to the gap after all other sources, no stated per-project cap. City funds posted June 1, 2026: HOME $5,000,000, Housing Trust Fund/Workforce Housing $1,000,000, Mixed Income Housing/Workforce Housing $2,500,000, PLHA $680,000 (about $9.2M). Applicants request gap funds without naming a source. January 2026 City pre-applications: Hotel Berry (Jamboree, preservation, $5.1M) invited; Florin Family Apartments (CCH, $5.1M) and Q Street Apartments (Community HousingWorks, $2.0M) invited; requests of $6.5M to $12M (Mercy 2601 5th Street, Danco 6779 Q Street, TWG 1220 H Street, Dos Rios) declined for insufficient funds. Projects must have 12 or more units.
- AMI requirement: 55-year regulatory agreement (HOME units per federal rules). SHRA minimum: at least 15% of units at or below 50% AMI and 5% at or below 30% AMI based on feasibility; regulated share at least proportional to SHRA share of total development cost; restricted rents at least 10% below market. Housing Trust Fund and Mixed Income fund money is limited to workforce households (up to 80% AMI, jobs-housing nexus). Priorities: preservation at risk, then new construction and nonresidential conversion (PSH and homeless housing, veterans, workforce 30% to 60% AMI, other), then rehab of regulated stock, then market-rate to affordable conversion.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: 2027 SHRA Multi-Family Loan and Mortgage Revenue Bond schedule (proposed): Pre-application January 4, 2027, full application March 1, 2027, environmental clearance May 3, 2027, SHRC June 23, 2027, Board/Council June 29, 2027; second round pre-application July 1, 2027, full application September 1, 2027, environmental clearance November 16, 2027, SHRC January 19, 2028, Board/Council January 25, 2028. 2027 schedule is Exhibit B to the 2027 SHRA budget item (SHRC heard Nov 4, 2026; County Board agenda Nov 3, 2026; City Council and Housing Authority hearing Nov 10, 2026); final adoption not yet confirmed. As of 2026-11-10 the SHRA multifamily page still says SHRA is not accepting pre-applications and links only the 2026 schedule and the June 1, 2026 funds-available notice; no 2027 funds-available notice or NOFA is posted. Phone (916) 440-1393.)
- Layering notes: This is the City-side pool parallel to the County SHRA record (Pass 2); a project uses one or the other based on location, both run on the same schedule and policies (2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies, amended July 29, 2026). Terms: up to 3% simple interest or the AFR, term up to 40 years from conversion or 55 years when senior public lenders require, 1.10x to 1.20x combined DSCR, payments deferred during construction and deferred developer fee repayment, residual receipts allowed; nonprofit managing general partner required; developer fee limited to $25,000/$15,000/$12,000 per unit tiers for non-tax-credit deals and deferred maximum fee for LIHTC deals. Federal HOME (12 or more units) and CDBG (8 or more units) trigger Davis-Bacon; SHRA treats state prevailing wage as applying unless the below-market loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years) fits. Stack with the City Zero-Dollar Rate impact fee reduction, Housing Impact Fee exemption at 40 du/acre, SacSewer fee waivers (County record) and Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento bonds. SHRA does not expect a project-based voucher RFP in 2026. SB 802 moves SHRA into the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency by Jan 1, 2028, so confirm the lender entity on 2027 and later commitments.
- Source: https://www.shra.org/multi-family-housing-financing-lending-resources/
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of Salinas

**CDBG, HOME and ESG entitlements, FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan (PY 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and Alisal Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area)**
- Agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
- Type: grant
- Typical award: FY 2026-27 resources $3,308,936: CDBG $2,196,140 plus $37,000 program income; HOME $844,248 plus $40,000 program income; ESG $191,548. CDBG recommendations: administration $446,628, Habitat for Humanity housing rehabilitation $440,000, Alisal NRSA sidewalks and streetlights $460,000, Chinatown neighborhood improvements $220,000, playground equipment $366,512, ECHO housing rights $100,000, Salinas Outreach and Response Team $200,000. HOME: $669,185 reserved for a shovel-ready affordable housing project (agency to be determined), $126,638 CHDO set-aside, $88,425 administration. ESG: $177,182 rapid rehousing. HOME-ARP $2,918,774 (2023) funds supportive services at Fairview Homekey ($1,190,337 to HACM, February 2026). The City is also the HCD ESG Administrative Entity for the Monterey/San Benito CoC.
- AMI requirement: HOME and CDBG income limits (80% AMI and below) with HOME rent and period-of-affordability rules; City loans typically carry 55-year covenants.

No FY 2027-28 NOFA notice found as of November 8, 2026.)
- Layering notes: Salinas is the only HOME participating jurisdiction in Monterey County besides the Urban County (county record covers unincorporated Monterey plus Gonzales, Greenfield, Marina and Sand City; Salinas is not in it). HOME and CDBG are usually committed through the City's multifamily NOFA (Vista de la Terraza $400,000 CDBG and $560,000 HOME; Casentini $3,267,000 HOME over several years) and require HUD NEPA clearance before covenants are signed. The Alisal NRSA designation (adopted June 17, 2025) relaxes CDBG public benefit rules in East Salinas. Section 108 loan guarantees are listed as a possible future tool. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 26-214) and the draft AAP PDF on legistar2.granicus.com.

**Density bonus (Zoning Code Section 37-50.060) and Zoning Code Update Phase 1 housing law amendments (2026)**
- Agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement and incentive, not a subsidy. Section 37-50.060 implements Government Code 65915 to 65917 with density bonuses, concessions (listed in subsection (k)) and parking reductions for very low, lower and moderate income, senior, day care and land donation projects, and adds a City density bonus for affordable senior housing (a 2014 senior project received a 100% bonus and 29% parking reduction). The Phase 1 Zoning Code Update ordinance (Planning Commission July 15, 2026; Council adoption August 2026, file 26-378) amended the density bonus, employee housing, two-unit development, ADU and emergency shelter provisions to match current state law and Housing Element Programs 4, 6, 7 and 14, and removed covered parking requirements for some residential uses. Phase 2 (objective design standards, General Plan consistency) is due mid-2027 and Phase 3 (new code) by end of 2027.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus law thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% affordable), 55-year rental covenants; affordable rent defined at 30% of 50% AMI (very low) and 30% of 60% AMI (lower).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Not applicable; by-right with the planning application. Watch the Vision Salinas 2040 General Plan draft (summer 2026) and Phase 2 zoning amendments (mid-2027) for new objective standards and West Area and Central Area Specific Plan sites (five tentative maps totaling 3,206 units in process in 2025).)
- Layering notes: No local trust fund money attaches to the bonus; it is the entitlement layer that is combined with the City's LHTF, HOME, PLHA and HSA loans. Bonus units are excluded when computing inclusionary obligations, and the Downtown inclusionary exemption plus the 2026 SB 423 streamlining (467 and 479 East Market Street hearing September 2025) make Chinatown and downtown the easiest sites. Code text read on the zoneomics mirror because municode and the City site block scripts; the Phase 1 ordinance staff report was read through the Salinas Legistar API.

**Housing Successor Agency (former Salinas Redevelopment Agency) Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund loans**
- Agency: City of Salinas as Housing Successor Agency; Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
- Type: loan

HSA funds are also pledged as part of the $100,000 a year ongoing revenue for the Salinas Local Housing Trust Fund.

HSA gap loans are awarded through the City's periodic housing NOFA (the Sun Rose loan came from the February 2022 NOFA; the most recent Multifamily NOFA opened June 24, 2025) and no new NOFA was announced in Salinas Legistar items through November 8, 2026.)

Combine with Monterey County Behavioral Health (MCHOME program) services funding for PSH, and with County HHAP for operating support (county records). Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 22-560, December 6, 2022 staff report) because the City website blocks scripts.
