**Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Salinas Municipal Code Chapter 17, Sections 17-8 to 17-13), rental housing impact fee, inclusionary housing trust fund and 2026-27 ordinance update (EPS study)**
- Agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Current ordinance (2017 amendment and guidelines): on-site inclusionary units apply only to for-sale developments of ten or more units, with three standard options (20% with 4% very low, 8% low, 4% moderate and 4% workforce at 160% AMI; 15% with 6% median, 6% moderate and 3% workforce ownership units; or 12% with 8% very low and 4% low rental units). Rental developments instead pay a per-square-foot rental housing impact fee set by fee resolution and must offer 12% of units to Housing Choice Voucher holders, unless they voluntarily provide affordable units in exchange for a City benefit. For-sale developers may pay a per-square-foot in-lieu fee at building permit. All fees go to the inclusionary housing trust fund. Exemptions include 100% affordable projects with 30-year restrictions and the Downtown (Central City Overlay) exemption added in 2022 (Section 17-8(d)). The City hired Economic and Planning Systems on February 1, 2026 to update the ordinance with a nexus and in-lieu fee study, a Technical Advisory Committee and a cost-recovery review fee; draft ordinance targeted for May 2027.
- AMI requirement: Very low (50% AMI), low (80%), median (100%), moderate (120%) and workforce (160%) tiers depending on option; inclusionary units must be comparable to market units and dispersed; first preference to Salinas residents and workers.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; fees due at building permit at the rate in the fee resolution then in effect. Housing and Land Use Committee received the update report October 20, 2026 (file 26-506); TAC outreach runs through spring 2027 and a draft ordinance is expected May 2027. Developers with pending projects should track the Phase 2 Zoning Code Update (mid-2027) as well.)
- Layering notes: Fee revenue feeds the inclusionary housing trust fund that, with the state LHTF award and HSA money, capitalizes the City's multifamily NOFA (record above). Salinas is the only Monterey County city that charges a rental housing impact fee instead of requiring on-site rental inclusionary units; the County's Chapter 18.40 ordinance (county record) does not apply inside city limits and the County's 2026 move to a fee-based program could influence the Salinas update. Density bonus units are excluded from the inclusionary count (Section 37-50.060). The ordinance text on municode is blocked to scripts; terms above come from the City's 2017 Inclusionary Housing Guidelines PDF (salinasca.prelive.opencities.com) and the October 2026 staff report read through the Salinas Legistar API. Verify current per-square-foot fee amounts in the FY 2026-27 master fee resolution.

PLHA pays land and predevelopment costs that HOME cannot (Saint George land $645,000), so it is usually the first City dollar in before a HOME or LHTF commitment. - Agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division (City Council sits as the Salinas LHTF Board of Directors)
- Type: loan

### City of San Carlos

**Below Market Rate (BMR) Ordinance (SCMC Chapter 18.16, revised June 2022)**
- Agency: City of San Carlos Community Development Department, Planning and Housing
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. 15% of units in market-rate developments: rental 10% very low plus 5% low income (or an option of 15% very low income to align with state density bonus law); ownership 10% moderate plus 5% low income, raised to 20% low income by the June 2022 revisions. On-site units required at 7 or more rental units and 5 or more ownership units; smaller projects pay an in-lieu fee.
- AMI requirement: Deed restrictions with City BMR eligibility rules (SCMC 18.16.080), San Carlos resident and worker preference, County income limits (2026 AMI $200,800 for four).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; in-lieu fee amount in the Master Fee Schedule (not opened).)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. The very low income rental tier makes San Carlos BMR units eligible to pair with HACSM PBVs; recent downtown projects at 1232 to 1360 Cherry Street used the ordinance's density bonus alignment. Source is the Housing Resources chapter of the 2023-2031 Housing Element.

- Agency: City of San Carlos Community Development Department, Housing Division (housing successor to the former Redevelopment Agency)
- Type: loan

Housing successor assets total about $9 million (817 Walnut Street ground lease and $10.4 million of loans receivable) with a slight cash deficit. A NOFA 25-26 is listed on the City housing page without details.

- Cycle: rolling (next: No open solicitation found; the City lists a NOFA 25-26 but the link resolves to the homepage. Contact the Housing Division at (650) 802-4265.)

San Carlos is cash-rich from life science linkage fees and land-rich downtown (Walnut Studios at 817 Walnut was the first City-financed project), so it funds projects at a much higher per-unit level than its neighbors; the per-square-foot linkage rate is in the Master Fee Schedule and was not confirmed this pass (codepublishing.com returned 403). ### City of San Diego

**Affordable Housing Density Bonus Regulations (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 3, Division 7) and ADU Home Density Bonus Program**
- Agency: San Diego Housing Commission (density bonus affordable unit review; Genevieve Hernandez, (619) 578-7588) and City Development Services Department
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to developments of five or more units. Local enhancements adopted March 6, 2018 (Housing SD): 10 percent density bonus for projects within the permitted building footprint, incentives or waivers available without requesting a bonus, 100 percent density bonus for micro-units within the footprint, and bonuses for sites with existing or recently expired rent restricted units. State bonuses up to 50 percent (80 percent or unlimited for 100 percent affordable) apply. ADU Home Density Bonus (SDMC 141.0302(d)): within a Sustainable Development Area one bonus ADU for each deed restricted affordable ADU with no fixed cap; outside a Sustainable Development Area a maximum of one bonus ADU and one affordable ADU; not available in RS-1-1 to RS-1-4 and RS-1-8 to RS-1-11 zones unless the site is High or Highest Resource and designated Residential; a Community Enhancement Fee applies. Permitting: 2,619 homes under the density bonus in 2024 (8,726 in 2021 to 2024); 653 ADUs under the ADU bonus in 2024 (892 in 2021 to 2024, 41 percent affordable). SDHC charges land use application fees (adjusted November 1, 2025).
- AMI requirement: Government Code 65915 tiers (5 percent very low, 10 percent low, 10 percent moderate for-sale, senior, 100 percent affordable); 55 years for rental units. ADU Home Density Bonus affordable ADUs: at least 10 years at very low income (rent at 30 percent of 50 percent AMI) or low income (30 percent of 60 percent AMI), or at least 15 years at moderate income (30 percent of 110 percent AMI) (SDMC 141.0302(d)).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; density bonus and ADU bonus regulations were amended in 2025 (O-21989) and the 2026 Land Development Code update; coastal zone versions lag Coastal Commission certification.)
- Layering notes: Developers choose between this and Complete Communities Housing Solutions (separate record). 100 percent affordable projects also get the Affordable Housing Expedite Program and Permit Now processing (separate record) and may use the Division 10 DIF waiver only if they elect Complete Communities. SDHC reviews affordability agreements for all programs and records them. Chula Vista, Oceanside, Escondido and Carlsbad ordinances simply conform to state law without these local enhancements. Read on sdhc.org (density bonus and ADU pages) and the City's 2025 Annual Report on Homes.
- Source: https://sdhc.org/doing-business-with-us/developers/density-bonus/
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Affordable, In-Fill Housing and Sustainable Buildings Expedite Program (Information Bulletin 538, Council Policy 600-27, SDMC 143.0915) and Affordable Housing Permit Now (Executive Order 2023-1)**
- Agency: City of San Diego Development Services Department, Expedite Team (DSD-ExpediteProgram@sandiego.gov) and Ministerial Project Managers (DSDMinisterialPM@sandiego.gov)
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Expedite program fees are waived for 100 percent affordable projects (otherwise fees per IB-503, capped at 40 percent of staff hourly billings). Discretionary review cycles cut to about half of standard (20 business day first review, 10 day subsequent reviews, completeness check in 5 days); ministerial expedite goal 25 percent faster. Permit Now: first review of 100 percent affordable and shelter building and engineering permits within 30 business days, dedicated project managers, collaborative review meetings; 26 projects completed by July 2026 and 3,094 homes permitted 2023 to 2024. Expedite program 2018 to 2024: 435 projects, 3,490 homes. Section 143.0920 allows deviations through a Process Two Neighborhood Development Permit.
- AMI requirement: Eligibility: 10 or more units with at least 10 percent at or below 60 percent AMI (rental) or 100 percent AMI (for-sale, or 15 percent at 120 percent AMI); SDHC-funded projects with 15 percent at 120 percent AMI; projects restricted at or below 80 percent AMI by public agreement; infill projects in Transit Priority Areas with all units at or below 150 percent AMI; Promise Zone projects. Projects paying the inclusionary fee are not eligible.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Rolling; request eligibility confirmation by email before submittal. IB 538 dated March 2023; Permit Now 3-year progress report issued March 2026.)
- Layering notes: Processing benefit rather than cash, but the fee waiver and timeline savings matter for TCAC readiness deadlines. Stack with the SDHC AHF NOFA, Bridge to Home and Complete Communities. Mandatory Initial Review is required for discretionary expedite projects. No comparable formal expedite program was found for Chula Vista, Oceanside or Carlsbad; Escondido offers pre-application consultation and expedited review under Housing Element Program 2.8.
- Source: https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletins/538
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Bridge to Home Program NOFA (Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund, PLHA and CDBG gap loans), Round 8 (2026)**
- Agency: City of San Diego Economic Development Department, Community Development Division, 1200 Third Ave., 14th Floor, San Diego 92101; Kristian Castro, KCastro@sandiego.gov, (619) 236-6700
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Round 8 (opened August 31, 2026, due October 19, 2026) offered $15 million: $10M LMIHAF for new construction of rental housing at 30 to 60 percent AMI and $5M PLHA restricted to units at or below 30 percent AMI for households experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Round 7 (February 3 to April 6, 2026) offered $16.5M and recommended three projects (430 homes). Round 6 (July 2025) about $16.65M for three projects (391 homes). Round 5 (2025) used $18.38M CDBG for acquisition (Mercado Apartments $15.275M for 222 units; Navajo Family $3.1M for 44 units). Seven rounds have recommended about $141.4M; typical awards $3.0M to $6.65M per project. LMIHAF cash balance $100.5M at June 30, 2025 (SB 341 report), FY25 deposits $8.19M and expenditures $13.37M.
- AMI requirement: 55 year covenants. LMIHAF: all assisted units at or below 80 percent AMI with at least 30 percent of units at or below 30 percent AMI and no more than 20 percent between 60 and 80 percent AMI (Health and Safety Code 34176.1). PLHA share only for 30 percent AMI units.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: No open round as of November 8, 2026; Round 8 applications closed in October 2026 and awards are pending. Round 9 not yet announced; developers must be on the Pre-Qualified Developer List (updated October 2026) or qualify through the rolling RFQ at least two weeks before a NOFA due date.)
- Layering notes: Two-step process: developer RFQ pre-qualification (Pre-Qualified Developer List updated October 7, 2026; small and emerging developers may partner), then NOFA. NOFA requires state prevailing wage on the whole project and 55 year covenants recorded senior to foreclosable liens. Pairs with SDHC AHF NOFA and SDHC bonds (separate records); the City prioritizes transit priority areas and Communities of Concern. The Affordable Housing Master Plan (2023 update) governs use of former redevelopment housing assets; since 2012, $233M has gone to over 4,000 units. Successor Agency surplus sites are offered by RFP (808 West Cedar RFP closed December 8, 2025; none open as of December 2025). County HCDS NOFAs normally exclude City of San Diego projects, so this and the SDHC AHF are the local layers. Prohousing: City designation (November 2022) lapsed January 2026 and renewal is pending (separate record).
- Source: https://www.sandiego.gov/economic-development/bridge-to-home
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**City of San Diego Affordable Housing Fund (Housing Trust Fund and Inclusionary Housing Fund, SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 5) and SDHC Affordable Housing and Permanent Supportive Housing NOFA (FY27 NOFA-27-01)**
- Agency: San Diego Housing Commission (SDHC), Real Estate Division, 1122 Broadway, Suite 300, San Diego 92101; NOFA contact Morgan Patterson, morganp@sdhc.org; NOFAs posted on the SDHC PlanetBids vendor portal
- Type: loan
- Typical award: FY27 NOFA-27-01 (released November 6, 2026) makes up to $22 million available (HOME plus Affordable Housing Fund) as residual receipts loans for new construction rental housing. FY 2027 Annual Plan: about $42.5 million AHF available July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 ($5.4M new fees and loan repayments plus $37.1M fund balances, of which $22.4M is already committed); Rental Housing Production allocation $30.39M including a $9.0M AHF share for the FY27 NOFA. Since 2018 SDHC has awarded more than $131 million to over 3,100 new affordable rental homes. Recent per project awards $1.0M to $2.85M (The Iris at San Ysidro, 99 units, $2.3M).
- AMI requirement: Minimum 55 years. HTF: at least 60 percent of funds for very low income (up to 50 percent AMI), no more than 20 percent for low income, no more than 10 percent for median income. IHF: priority to new construction of units for very low and low income households; rents at or below 30 percent of income, generally at least 10 percent below market.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: FY27 NOFA-27-01 is open (released by SDHC in November 2026); the application due date is set in the NOFA on the SDHC PlanetBids vendor portal (SDHC-specific registration required) and is not stated in the public release.)
- Layering notes: Largest city-controlled gap source in the county. Stacks under 4 percent and 9 percent LIHTC, SDHC bonds (separate record), SDHC project-based vouchers through the same NOFA, and County HCDS NOFA 2026-03 money only where a project sits in the City but County IHTF rarely funds City of San Diego sites. The City's Bridge to Home LMIHAF and PLHA NOFA (separate record) is run by the Economic Development Department, not SDHC, and projects commonly take both. HOME funds awarded to the City are administered by SDHC and folded into the same NOFA. AHF also funds ADU construction loans up to $250,000 at 3 percent for low income homeowners (7 year affordability) and homeless programs. FY27 plan and FY25 annual report read on sdhc.org.
- Source: https://sdhc.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/FY27-AHF-Plan.pdf

**City of San Diego CDBG entitlement NOFA (FY2028 RFQ and RFP cycle) and HOME entitlement administered through SDHC**
- Agency: City of San Diego Economic Development Department, Community Development Division, 1200 Third Ave., Suite 1400, MS 56D, San Diego 92101; CDBG@sandiego.gov, (619) 236-6700; HOME administered by SDHC
- Type: grant
- Typical award: FY2027 CDBG competitive categories: public services about $1.29M, community and economic development about $2.72M, nonprofit facility improvement $2.0M (March 2026 funding decision memos). Capital funds for affordable housing acquisition are deployed through Bridge to Home rounds (Round 5 used $18.38M CDBG for two acquisitions). City HOME: in FY2026, 113 of 709 affordable rental units built were HOME funded; HOME is combined with Affordable Housing Fund money in the SDHC NOFA.
- AMI requirement: CDBG national objective (low and moderate income benefit); HOME units at or below 60 percent AMI rents for 15 to 20 years or longer under the SDHC NOFA (55 years).
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: FY2028 CDBG RFQ released October 5, 2026, RFQ responses due November 6, 2026 (5 pm), RFP to qualified organizations December 7, 2026, mandatory workshop December 8, proposals due January 15, 2027 (5 pm), CPAB scores March 5, 2027, Council action April to June 2027 with the FY2028 Annual Action Plan.)
- Layering notes: Developers rarely apply to the CDBG public services round; the relevant path is Bridge to Home (CDBG acquisition) and the SDHC NOFA (HOME). Federal cross-cutting rules (Davis-Bacon, NEPA, Section 3) attach. The County's Urban County CDBG and HOME Consortium (county records) do not cover the City of San Diego, which is its own entitlement and participating jurisdiction. FY2026 CAPER and FY2027 Annual Action Plan are posted on the CDBG page.

**Complete Communities Housing Solutions (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 3, Division 10): FAR bonus, Development Impact Fee waiver and Neighborhood Enhancement Fee**
- Agency: City of San Diego Development Services Department and City Planning Department; SDHC reviews affordable unit compliance
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Optional incentive program within Sustainable Development Areas (sites zoned or designated for 20 or more units per acre, or within one-quarter mile of a rail station; SDMC 143.1002) replacing density limits with floor area ratio tiers (Tier 1 Downtown no FAR maximum, Tier 2 FAR 8.0, Tier 3 FAR 6.5, Tier 4 FAR 4.0, plus 1.5 FAR for family-sized units). Required (143.1015(a)): rental projects must restrict, excluding bonus units, 15 percent of units at 50 percent AMI rents plus 10 percent at 60 percent AMI plus 15 percent at 120 percent AMI (40 percent total), or alternatively 40 percent at 50 percent AMI, 100 percent at 60 percent AMI, or 100 percent moderate (half at 80 percent AMI, half at 120 percent AMI); for-sale tiers are in 143.1016; naturally affordable units must be replaced. Section 143.1010(f): waiver of Development Impact Fees for all covenant restricted affordable units, up to 30 percent of units of 500 square feet or less (if at least 10 percent are three bedroom units), and three bedroom units restricted at or below 150 percent AMI, when the project reaches at least 120 percent of base maximum density. Neighborhood Enhancement Fee (Resolution R-313282; about $9.00 per square foot of lot area per the program page) or a public space on sites of 25,000 square feet or more; the fee is waived only when 100 percent of units (excluding managers units) are restricted at or below 50 percent AMI (143.1010(g)). Permitting: 1,917 homes in 2024 and 3,372 homes 2021 to 2024.
- AMI requirement: Deed restricted on-site units for very low, low and moderate income households (up to 120 percent AMI) for 55 years; right to return and priority preference (75 percent of affordable units) for Communities of Concern residents.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Ministerial review; January 10, 2024 executive order requires departmental review within 30 days. The 2026 Land Development Code update (adopted mid 2026) adjusted FAR bonuses and DIF provisions; verify current 143.1010 text before relying on the waiver.)
- Layering notes: Can be combined with the inclusionary requirement (the required units satisfy both) but not with the state density bonus on the same project in most cases; developers choose Complete Communities or the Affordable Housing Density Bonus (separate record). DIF waiver is a City fee waiver and may be treated as public funds for Labor Code 1720 purposes; confirm with DIR. Expedite Program and Affordable Housing Permit Now apply to qualifying projects. Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov; program page on sandiego.gov/complete-communities.
- Source: https://docs.sandiego.gov/municode/MuniCodeChapter14/Ch14Art03Division10.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Housing Impact Fee (commercial linkage fee) funding the San Diego Housing Trust Fund (SDMC Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 6)**
- Agency: City of San Diego Facilities Financing (calculation) and Development Services Department (collection); San Diego Housing Commission administers the resulting Housing Trust Fund
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Charged per square foot on new office, hotel, research and development, retail and other commercial development; the 2014 compromise ordinance (adopted November 10, 2014) phased rates to $2.12 per square foot for office, $1.28 for hotel and retail, and $0.80 for research and development, with exemptions for manufacturing, warehouse and certain Enterprise Zone uses and an option to dedicate land in lieu of the fee. Revenue: FY25 collections $1.78M (39 percent above budget); FY27 projected $1.36M in new HTF revenue; projected HTF balance $6.38M entering FY27.
- AMI requirement: Fee revenue must serve very low, low and median income households (at least 60 percent of HTF to very low income).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Paid at building permit. SDHC adopts the Affordable Housing Fund Annual Plan each spring; FY27 plan allocated $2.5M of HTF to the FY27 NOFA and $150,000 to transitional housing grants.)
- Layering notes: The HTF has been a declining share of SDHC's local money; the Inclusionary Housing Fund is now about five times larger. HTF money is the most flexible local source (loans, grants, indirect assistance) and is used for the SDHC NOFA, homeless housing grants and administration. No comparable city linkage fee exists in Chula Vista, Oceanside, Escondido or Carlsbad (Carlsbad's trust fund collects housing impact fees under a different code section). Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov; the current fee amount should be confirmed with Facilities Financing because the code table shows the 2014 phase-in schedule.
- Source: https://docs.sandiego.gov/municode/MuniCodeChapter09/Ch09Art08Division06.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Inclusionary Affordable Housing Regulations and Inclusionary In Lieu Fee (SDMC Chapter 14, Article 2, Division 13; O-21167 as amended through O-22109)**
- Agency: San Diego Housing Commission (administration, monitoring and Inclusionary Housing Fund; Genevieve Hernandez, genevieveh@sdhc.org, (619) 578-7588) and City Development Services Department (DS-530 checklist, fee collection)
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to residential development of 10 or more units outside the Coastal Overlay Zone, 5 or more units inside the Coastal Overlay Zone, and condominium conversions of 2 or more units (SDMC 142.1302). Rental: at least 10 percent of total units for very low or low income households at rents not exceeding 30 percent of 60 percent of AMI (fully effective July 1, 2024). For-sale: 10 percent at median income (100 percent AMI) or 15 percent at moderate income (120 percent AMI). In lieu fee $25.00 per square foot of net building area of unrestricted market-rate units effective July 1, 2024, updated annually by the ENR Los Angeles Construction Cost Index ($12.73 for projects deemed complete before July 1, 2020). Other compliance: off-site units, rehabilitation or conversion of existing units, SRO or hotel rooms to 55-year affordable units, land donation. North City Future Urbanizing Area projects are exempt from this Division and follow the Framework Plan inclusionary requirement (20 percent). IHF fee revenue FY25 $17.76M (255 percent above budget); FY27 projected new IHF revenue $4.04M.
- AMI requirement: Rental inclusionary units restricted at least 55 years; on-site affordable units count toward state density bonus; developments restricted at or below 80 percent AMI by agreement are exempt.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at permit. The fee rate is set when the development permit, subdivision or building permit application is deemed complete (whichever is earliest) and is paid on or before the first residential building permit (SDMC 142.1306). Division 13 was amended June 15, 2026 by O-22109 (effective July 15, 2026, not yet effective in the Coastal Overlay Zone); Information Bulletin 532 revised August 2026.)
- Layering notes: Fees feed the Inclusionary Housing Fund, the larger of the two Affordable Housing Fund accounts (about $30.7M projected balance entering FY27) and the main source of the SDHC NOFA (record above). Projects that pay the fee are not eligible for the Affordable Housing Expedite Program; projects providing on-site units get expedite processing and may stack state density bonus and Complete Communities Housing Solutions FAR bonuses. Compare Chula Vista (10 percent at 20 or more units), Carlsbad (15 percent at 7 or more units) and Oceanside (15 percent at 3 or more units); the unincorporated County ordinance is a separate county record. Code PDF read on docs.sandiego.gov and the SDHC inclusionary page.
- Source: https://docs.sandiego.gov/municode/MuniCodeChapter14/Ch14Art02Division13.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**SDHC Multifamily Housing Revenue Bond Program (Housing Authority of the City of San Diego conduit bonds, Policy 300.301)**
- Agency: San Diego Housing Commission, Real Estate Division, Multifamily Housing Bond Program, 1122 Broadway, Suite 300, San Diego 92101; Colin Miller, (619) 578-7429, colinm@sdhc.org; MultifamilyBondProgram@sdhc.org
- Type: bond
- Typical award: Conduit tax-exempt private activity bonds sized to project debt; no City or SDHC liability. Application: Bond Inducement Application (DocuSign), $3,000 application fee and $10,000 deposit (refunded at closing, when issuer and ongoing administrative fees apply), plus notarized Developer Disclosure Statement. Issuances since 1982; program policy enacted 1989.

- Layering notes: SDHC is the issuer of choice inside the City; CMFA and CSCDA issuances are also used with City TEFRA approval (County TEFRA practice is a separate county record). Pairs with 4 percent LIHTC and the SDHC AHF NOFA and Bridge to Home loans. Chula Vista's Housing Authority now acts as issuer in most cases within that city (separate record); Oceanside has issued only occasionally (last 2016); Escondido and Carlsbad rely on JPAs.

- Agency: City of San Diego City Planning Department, Prohousing@sandiego.gov

### City of San Jose

**Affordable Housing Impact Fee (Chapter 17.14, suspended 2021) and Commercial Linkage Fee (Chapter 5.11)**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. AHIF: $17.00 per livable square foot on market-rate rental projects at adoption (2014), escalating 2.4 percent a year to $20.08 when suspended for projects first approved on or after June 29, 2021 (Resolution 80149). Cumulative AHIF revenue and interest $25.6 million; fund balance $11.4 million at June 30, 2025, all to be committed through the Gap Financing Program. CLF (Ordinance 30475, September 22, 2020): FY 2025-26 rates are $17.86 per square foot for office at or above 100,000 square feet downtown and nearby (lower tiers for smaller office), hotel $5.95, industrial over 100,000 square feet $3.57, warehouse $5.95, residential care $7.15, with reduced rates outside downtown. Cumulative CLF revenue $6.1 million, to be allocated through the Gap Financing Program.
- AMI requirement: Fee revenue funds housing for extremely low, very low, low and moderate income households under City regulatory agreements (55 years or longer).
- Cycle: closed/inactive (next: No direct application; the funds are awarded through the Gap Financing Program rolling RFP. Next Mitigation Fee Act annual report due to Council in late 2026.)
- Layering notes: Both funds are small relative to LMIHAF and are blended into Gap Financing awards. The CLF was adopted at well below the Keyser Marston nexus maximum and office construction has been weak, so expect only a few million dollars a year. The AHIF was replaced by extending the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance to rental projects of 10 or more units. Compare with Mountain View and Sunnyvale, whose commercial linkage fees have generated far larger balances. sanjoseca.gov blocked; the FY 2024-25 annual report memo was read from Legistar.

**Alternative financing frameworks for affordable housing (Gap Financing plus IHO, PAB plus master-lease, production incentives plus master-lease)**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Council resolution of September 1, 2026 authorizing the Housing Director to implement four mixed-financing models: (1) Gap Financing Program loans in exchange for deeper inclusionary set-asides (example: 10 percent of units at 50 percent AMI instead of 5 percent at 60 and 5 percent at 80); (2) private activity bonds combined with master-lease financing; (3) production incentive programs (MHIP) combined with master-lease financing; (4) master-lease financing combined with the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance. Target rents 40 to 110 percent AMI. No new dollars; uses existing Gap Financing, bond and incentive tools.

- Layering notes: Relevant to developers of mixed-income towers (prevailing wage already assumed) and to nonprofit or public master lessees. Models borrow from the Bay Area Housing Finance Authority and CalHFA middle-income work; they will compete with the Multifamily Housing Incentive Program pipeline for the same market-rate projects. Prohousing: San Jose applied for HCD Prohousing Designation in June 2023 (memo read); current designation status was not confirmed this pass, verify on HCD's designated jurisdictions list. sanjoseca.gov blocked; memo read from Legistar. Audit 2026-11-08 funding_type: classed as loan because Model 1 is a Gap Financing loan and the master-lease models use City funding expected to be repaid on exit; no new grant dollars.

- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department, Residential Development, Production and Preservation
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Construction-permanent and acquisition loans from the Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund, Inclusionary Fee Fund, Measure E Real Property Transfer Tax Fund and impact fee funds. The April 14, 2025 joint New Construction/Preservation RFP was backed by a $50 million commitment; the June 2025 Round 1 NOFA addendum has produced three awards so far. 2025 awards: $48.3 million for Berryessa TOD and Gateway Tower (415 units); Gateway Tower $38.44 million total ($174,727 per unit on 220 units, later revised to $25.56 million after CalHFA MIP and state credits); 1510 North 1st Street hotel conversion $5.7 million (58 units, October 2026); Capitol Station $8.4 million LMIHAF. **Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, Municipal Code Chapter 5.08, in-lieu fees and Surplus Credits Exchange (2026 amendments)**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to residential developments of 10 or more units (threshold lowered from 20 in 2021). On-site rental options after the January 27, 2026 amendments: 5 percent at 60 percent AMI, 5 percent at 80 percent AMI and 5 percent at 110 percent AMI (15 percent total); the former 10 percent at 30 percent AMI alternative was removed. For-sale: 15 percent at 120 percent AMI with the price cap raised to 120 percent AMI. Off-site rental: 30 percent (10 percent each at 60, 80 and 100 percent AMI); off-site for-sale 25 percent at 110 percent AMI. In-lieu fee is set per square foot in the annual Schedule of Fees; about $50 million in in-lieu fees collected from 15 fee-only projects since March 2021 ($38.2 million fee-only plus $12.4 million mixed compliance). Fees flow to the Inclusionary Fee Fund, which is a Gap Financing Program source ($4.3 million committed to Gateway Tower in 2025). Pipeline: 73 projects, 12,900 units, 1,900 affordable.
- AMI requirement: Inclusionary rental units restricted for 55 years (reduced from 99 years in 2026 to match TCAC and state density bonus terms). 100 percent affordable developments at or below 100 percent AMI now comply by recording an abbreviated City covenant that mirrors their TCAC, HCD or CDLAC regulatory agreements instead of a full Inclusionary Housing Agreement.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Ordinance adopted January 27, 2026 and effective in 2026. The Surplus Credits Exchange (Section 5.08.540) will get a 12-month performance review; check the Housing Department for exchange rules and current in-lieu fee rates (set each June in the Schedule of Fees and Charges).)
- Layering notes: For affordable developers the key uses are: (1) the Inclusionary Fee Fund as a gap source, (2) the 2026 Surplus Credits Exchange, where a 100 percent affordable or mixed-income project that exceeds its requirement can sell credits (room-count equivalency) to market-rate projects, a potential new equity-like revenue stream, and (3) streamlined compliance for 100 percent affordable projects. Alternative Financing Model 1 (August 2026) pairs Gap Financing loans with deeper inclusionary set-asides (for example 10 percent at 50 percent AMI) in tower and wrap projects. Market-rate projects in the Multifamily Housing Incentive Program pay a $0 in-lieu fee if they provide 5 percent at up to 110 percent AMI on site, which reduces fee revenue to the fund. State density bonus can be layered on inclusionary units. sanjoseca.gov blocked; memo and ordinance read from Legistar.
- Source: https://legistar.granicus.com/sanjose/attachments/80d86249-fa6c-42b1-8689-e3f55e732331.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF), Housing Successor to the San Jose Redevelopment Agency**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department as Housing Successor
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Ending balance June 30, 2025: $95,884,306. Deposits in FY 2024-25: $22,478,762 (loan repayments and interest). FY 2024-25 expenditures $24.1 million, of which $12.5 million housing development (mostly extremely low income units) and $11.4 million monitoring and administration. Gross value of Housing Successor assets $721 million (loan portfolio and land). Recent LMIHAF commitments: $17.97 million construction-permanent plus $2.17 million acquisition for Gateway Tower, $8.4 million Capitol Station, $5.7 million 1510 North 1st Street.
- AMI requirement: Dissolution Law targets: at least 30 percent of expenditures for rental housing at or below 30 percent AMI and no more than 20 percent for 60 to 80 percent AMI, measured over five-year periods; City covenants of 55 years or longer.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Funds are awarded through the rolling RFP and NOFA addenda described in the Gap Financing Program record; next addendum expected 2026. Annual Housing Successor report is presented each March with the Housing Element APR.)
- Layering notes: The largest and most stable local pool in the county at about $96 million, replenished by about $20 million per year of loan repayments as older RDA loans mature. Draws require a Council appropriation from the Housing Project Reserve. Stacks with County Measure A, SCCHA project-based vouchers, 4 percent credits and CalHFA MIP. Program income rules make it less flexible than inclusionary fee funds for moderate income units. sanjoseca.gov blocked; the Housing Successor Annual Report was read as an attachment to the March 2026 APR Council item.

**Measure E Real Property Transfer Tax (Municipal Code Chapter 4.59) and Council Policy 1-18 Section 22 spending allocations**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department and City Manager's Budget Office; Real Property Transfer Tax Fund
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Transfer tax on sales above $2.3 million (threshold indexed from $2 million as of July 1, 2025): 0.75 percent from $2 million to $5 million, 1.0 percent from $5 million to $10 million, 1.5 percent above $10 million. About $225 million collected July 2020 through mid 2023. FY 2025-26 revenue estimate $55.0 million, FY 2026-27 $60.0 million. Original policy (April 2022) directed 40 percent to extremely low income housing, 30 percent low income, 5 percent moderate income, 10 percent homelessness prevention, 15 percent homeless support. The June 10, 2025 revision allows up to 90 percent of revenue after 5 percent administration for homeless sheltering and interim housing, with only the remainder for new or preserved affordable housing; the FY 2025-26 plan puts $0 of new revenue into affordable housing development, and the same June 2025 spending plan programs FY 2026-27 and ongoing revenue ($60.0 million) as $3.0 million administration, $5.7 million homelessness prevention, $51.3 million homeless sheltering and support and $0 for affordable housing. Prior-year Measure E reserves are still being drawn for development, for example $14 million for the Gateway Tower land acquisition (September 2025).
- AMI requirement: When used for development: new or preserved rental housing for extremely low (30 percent AMI) and low income households under City regulatory agreements; previously set by AMI category in Policy 1-18 Section 22.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No standalone Measure E NOFA and no open round as of November 9, 2026. The June 10, 2025 spending plan allocates $0 of FY 2026-27 and ongoing Measure E revenue to affordable housing; any housing share would have to come from a later annual budget (next adoption June 2027). Remaining prior-year Measure E reserves reach developers only through Gap Financing Program awards; verify balances with the Housing Department.)
- Layering notes: Measure E was the City's largest discretionary housing source from 2020 to 2024 and funded many Gap Financing Program awards. Expect limited new Measure E development money through at least FY 2026-27 because the General Fund shortfall shifted $39.2 million (rising to $42.8 million) of homelessness costs into this fund. Developers should underwrite LMIHAF and inclusionary fee funds first and treat Measure E as upside. A Measure E transfer tax refund pilot for qualifying nonprofit purchases (Section 4.59.230) ran July 2021 through June 30, 2024 with one application; it is now expired. Documents read via Legistar attachments because sanjoseca.gov is blocked. Audit 2026-11-08 funding_type: classed as loan because the development share reaches projects as Gap Financing Program loans (the June 2025 memo cites about $60 million of prior-year Measure E and other housing funds for a Gap Financing NOFA); the shelter share is City-operated spending, not a developer source.

**Multifamily Housing Incentive Program (MHIP), construction tax reductions and inclusionary in-lieu fee waiver (Municipal Code Sections 4.46.039.13 and 4.47.098)**
- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department with Planning, Building and Code Enforcement, Public Works and Finance
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Phase I (projects that apply by February 28, 2027 and pull building permits by that date, capacity expanded from 1,800 to 3,600 units on January 27, 2026): 50 percent reduction of the Building and Structure Construction Tax (1.54 percent to 0.77 percent of valuation), 50 percent reduction of the Commercial, Residential and Mobile Home Park Construction Tax (2.42 percent to 1.21 percent), reduced inclusionary requirement of 5 percent of units at 100 percent AMI (or up to 110 percent AMI) and a $0 inclusionary in-lieu fee. Phase II (after capacity or March 2027): 25 percent Building and Structure tax reduction (to 1.16 percent) plus the inclusionary benefits. Approved waivers range from $4.07 million (498 West San Carlos, 278 units) to $6.93 million (3896 Stevens Creek Phase 1, 311 units, September 2026). Five projects with 1,444 units started construction under the program by January 2026.
- AMI requirement: Market-rate high-density projects (50 or more units per acre in growth areas) providing at least 5 percent of units affordable at up to 100 or 110 percent AMI; recorded affordability restriction required. Financial infeasibility finding under Municipal Code Section 14.10.310 and the 2025 Cost of Residential Development Study.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Phase I application deadline February 28, 2027; building permit must be obtained by February 28, 2027 for the 50 percent reductions. Each waiver requires a Council public hearing under Government Code 53083.)
- Layering notes: Not a subsidy for 100 percent affordable projects, which generally are exempt from these construction taxes anyway, but it is the City's main production incentive for mixed-income market-rate towers and wraps and it shapes the inclusionary pipeline (lower on-site percentages, zero in-lieu fee revenue). Alternative Financing Model 3 (August 2026) pairs MHIP incentives with master-lease financing so that a public or nonprofit master lessee can take down units at 80 to 110 percent AMI. Developers combining MHIP with state density bonus should confirm the 5 percent at 100 percent AMI units count toward density bonus moderate income thresholds. sanjoseca.gov blocked; staff memo read from Legistar.

- Agency: City of San Jose Housing Department and Finance Department
- Type: bond
- Typical award: City-issued tax-exempt multifamily housing revenue bonds and notes for 4 percent LIHTC projects, for example Berryessa TOD (March 2026), 525 North Capitol (June 2025) and La Moraga refunding (July 2025). Policy 1-16 was amended April 28, 2026 to streamline readiness requirements, financing team selection, private placements and alternative structures, and to prioritize developments leveraging substantial non-City subsidy, preservation of at-risk units and permanent supportive housing. City fees and procedures are moving to an administrative procedures document.

County TEFRA approvals cover unincorporated projects only. sanjoseca.gov blocked; memo read from Legistar.

### City of San Juan Bautista

**Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Zoning Code Chapter 11-09) and affordable housing in-lieu fee account**
- Agency: City of San Juan Bautista Planning Department (contract planning staff; City Hall 311 Second Street)
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Residential projects of six or more units (the Housing Element describes the rental threshold as five or more) must reserve one affordable unit for every five market-rate units (about 16.7% of base units, calculated before any density bonus) for very low or low income households, for sale or as rentals (Section 11-09-400); fractions may be met with a partial in-lieu fee. In-lieu payment of the whole obligation is allowed only at the City Council's discretion after a Planning Commission recommendation (11-09-500); the per-unit fee formula (11-09-505) is the San Benito County median home sales price for the prior fourth quarter minus the maximum affordable three-bedroom sales price, divided across all project units and paid at building permit. Fees go to a separate interest-bearing account used solely to provide housing opportunities for very low and low income households anywhere in the City (11-09-510). Off-site and joint-venture off-site rental compliance allowed on an infeasibility showing (11-09-600).
- AMI requirement: Very low (50% AMI) and low (80% AMI) households by San Benito County HUD limits; for-sale and rental reserved units deed restricted for at least 55 years; rental units may not convert to condominiums during the restriction; reserved units must match the design and bedroom and square footage proportions of market units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; reserved units built before or with market units and in proportion by phase. The 2023-2031 Housing Element (certified by HCD) adds a program to update the inclusionary provisions and notes that most buildable lots fall under the six-unit threshold, so no project has yet triggered the requirement; fee reductions or waivers have been negotiated in development agreements.)
- Layering notes: The in-lieu account has no reported balance (the ordinance was adopted in 2007 and the Housing Element says the City has no staff or financial resources for a stand-alone housing program), so it is not a realistic gap source. The one-in-five requirement is roughly comparable to San Benito County's 15% on-site standard but with deeper targeting (very low and low only, no moderate). Mixed-use infill in the downtown and gateway districts is the City's moderate-income strategy; exclusively residential new construction on commercial-only Mixed Use parcels is allowed only when 100% affordable, which pairs well with a 100% affordable density bonus project. Layer with San Benito County PLHA (the City passes its own PLHA allocation to the County for homeless services under an MOU), County HHAP and state programs; Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz PBVs cover San Benito County. Code text read on the zoneomics mirror.
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/san-juan-bautista-CA/chapter_10
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**State density bonus implementation and city housing finance capacity (2023-2031 Housing Element programs on density bonus, PLHA and CDBG)**
- Agency: City of San Juan Bautista Planning Department and City Manager's office
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: No local enhancement. The adopted and HCD-certified 2023-2031 Housing Element (Final No. 5, January 20, 2026) states the City applies California Density Bonus Law directly (described as up to 35%; current Government Code 65915 allows up to 50% or more) with incentives such as reduced parking, and offers up to a 50% bonus in the Mixed-Use District for special needs and 100% affordable projects. Program 3.8 commits to revising the local density bonus ordinance to match state law by December 2026. Financial resources: the City intends to use over $320,000 of PLHA for an ADU Amnesty Program and has passed part of its PLHA (2019 allocation, $75,999 of a $455,999 2019-2025 plan) to San Benito County for homeless services; it has no CDBG, HOME or redevelopment funds but plans to apply for competitive CDBG and holds inclusionary in-lieu fees.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus law thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, senior, 100% affordable); inclusionary units under Chapter 11-09 are counted before bonus units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No application deadline; state density bonus applies on request. Confirm whether the Program 3.8 density bonus ordinance update (due December 2026) has been adopted.)
- Layering notes: Explicit negative finding: San Juan Bautista has no local housing trust fund, no fee waiver program, no city NOFA and no city-controlled development funds beyond the Chapter 11-09 in-lieu account. Development capacity is constrained by water and sewer (a sewer force main to Hollister is a City project) and by the 8 to 15 units per acre Mixed-Use zoning; Program 3.13 commits to raising the Mixed-Use designation to 16 to 24 units per acre by December 2026. The only city-level tools are the inclusionary ordinance, state density bonus and SB 35 streamlining; capital must come from San Benito County (PLHA, HHAP, CMFA conduit bonds), Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz PBVs and state programs. The City's Housing Element page states the element is adopted and certified by HCD.
- Source: https://san-juan-bautista.ca.us/document_center/Planning/Housing element/SJB HE_FINAL_NO 5_1.20.26_CLEAN_VERSION.pdf?t=202605181642440
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, San Leandro Zoning Code Chapter 6.04 (Ordinance 2004-023, amended 2020-002), in-lieu fee and Affordable Housing Trust Fund (6.04.156)**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department, Housing Services Division, 835 East 14th Street; housing@sanleandro.org, (510) 577-6006
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. At least 15% of units in residential developments must be inclusionary units for moderate, low or very low income households (density bonus units excluded from the base); for-sale projects of 2 to 6 units may pay an in-lieu fee equal to (median San Leandro sales price minus affordable ownership cost) times a fractional unit of 0.30 to 0.90; larger projects may combine fees with off-site alternatives only with approval. Exempt: for-sale projects and condo conversions under 2 units and rental projects under 4 units. Fees, condo conversion fees and loan repayments go to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. FY 2025 AHTF revenue $24,682 (no in-lieu fees), balance $336,166 at June 30, 2025 (FY 2024 restated to $311,484 after audit). Recent BMR production: Centro Callan (10 BMR rental units), Poppy Lane (3 BMR homes).
- AMI requirement: 15% of units for moderate, low or very low income households; rental inclusionary units subject to recorded covenants administered under the BMR Procedural Manual (SLMC 19.172.030).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at map or planning approval; the 2023-2031 Housing Element commits to an economic feasibility study and ordinance amendments during the cycle (not yet scheduled).)
- Layering notes: The AHTF is too small to fund projects on its own; it has covered predevelopment grants and a site acquisition contribution. The ordinance predates AB 1505 and still exempts small rental projects; developers of rental projects with 4 or more units owe 15% on-site, which is above Hayward's and Fremont's rental percentages and a cost consideration for mixed-income deals. **Park Facilities Development Impact Fee exemption and 50% reduction for affordable units (Administrative Code Section 8.8.121, Council item 25-347, July 2025)**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department and Recreation and Parks
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Park impact fees restructured in July 2025 from per-unit-type ($18,074 per multifamily unit in FY 2024-25) to unit-size tiers: under 550 sq ft $6,052; 550 to 750 sq ft $7,565; 751 to 1,150 sq ft $11,600; 1,151 to 1,650 sq ft $16,140; 1,651 to 1,950 sq ft $20,679; over 1,950 sq ft $25,723 (land acquisition plus improvement components, CPI and ENR indexed). ### City of San Luis Obispo

**Affordable Housing Incentives and local density bonus (Municipal Code Chapter 17.140; Ord. 1705, 2021)**
- Agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department (Director approval; review authority resolution for alternative incentives)
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement-based entitlement, not a subsidy. Density bonus of 20% to 50% per Tables 8-3 and 8-4 (10% low income earns 20%, rising to 50% at 24% low income; 5% very low earns 20%); the Director may approve a bonus above 50% at the developer's request. One to three incentives or concessions on the state schedule, and alternative incentives listed in Section 17.140.070 include deferral of application and development review processing fees, deferral of park land in-lieu fees or dedication, mixed-use zoning, reduced site standards and parking. Housing Element Program 2.14 commits the City to support bonuses above the 35% state base; the City approved more than 15 density bonus requests in 2018-2020.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, 100% senior, 10% transitional foster youth, disabled veterans or homeless); affordable units covenanted per state law through an affordable housing agreement (Section 17.140.080). Applies to projects of five or more units including mixed-use.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Not applicable; requested with the planning application.)
- Layering notes: Local enhancement beyond state law: Director can approve bonuses above 50% and fee deferrals count as incentives. Projects using a density bonus are exempt from Chapter 17.138 inclusionary requirements. Base densities in the City's high-density zones are 24 or more units per acre before bonus, and the Downtown Flexible Density Program (Chapter 17.141) allows small units (150 to 600 sq ft) outside the inclusionary ordinance. Stack with AHF awards and the City impact fee deferral; the County's Regional Housing Incentive Program (Title 22 Section 22.12.010) applies only to unincorporated land. - Agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department, Housing Programs (Council awards)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Gap grants and below-market loans at Council discretion under adopted criteria (Resolution 9263, 2001 Series). Housing Element history: $10,450,954 of in-lieu funds granted, loaned or committed to 464 deed-restricted units since the 1999 inclusionary ordinance; Bishop Street Studios (34 units) received $1,595,500 combined AHF loan, impact fee deferral loan and CDBG loan; $330,000 grant to TMHA for a 6-unit acquisition-rehab. Not confirmed on an agency source in the audit: a $2 million January 2020 approval for a 108-unit project; a 2023 Council resolution approving $3.2 million to HASLO for 736 Orcutt Road ($2.0 million) and 279 Bridge Street ($1.2 million); and $750,000 of 2024 Prohousing Incentive funds routed through the AHF. Housing Element target: support at least 4 new affordable developments during the planning period.
- AMI requirement: Extremely low, very low, low and moderate income; deed restrictions of 55 years rental and 45 years ownership under City Affordable Housing Standards. Housing Element Program 2.5 directs the fund to projects that would not be feasible without AHF support and to production efficiency.
- Cycle: rolling (next: unknown, verify with agency. No formal NOFA; developers request awards through the Housing Programs Coordinator (housing@slocity.org) and awards go to Council by resolution, usually timed to TCAC or CDLAC rounds.)
- Layering notes: Largest city-controlled housing fund in the county. Revenue is the Chapter 17.138 in-lieu fee and Chapter 4.60 commercial linkage fee plus shared-equity recapture; the City also receives its own CDBG share through the Urban County (county record: Urban County Action Plan NOFA, due October 30, 2026 for the 2027 program year) and has layered CDBG loans with AHF awards. Typical stack for a City of SLO LIHTC deal: AHF grant or loan, City impact fee deferral loan (separate record), County Title 29 or Regional Housing Fund, HASLO project-based vouchers, SLO County Housing Trust Fund predevelopment loan, then state sources. HCD-hosted Housing Element was the only agency document that could be opened; slocity.org (403) and the City eScribe agenda host pub-slocity.escribemeetings.com (filestream 403, JS-only listings) could not be read, so current fund balance and 2025-2026 awards are unconfirmed.
- Source: https://www.hcd.ca.gov/housing-elements/docs/san-luis-obispo-6th-adopted072321.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Development services fee waiver and citywide development impact fee deferral loans for affordable units (Housing Element incentives table; Chapter 4.56 impact fee deferral)**
- Agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department and Finance Department
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Residential projects meeting City affordable housing standards for extremely low, very low and low income households are exempt from all planning, engineering and building review, processing and permit fees and water and sewer meter hook-up fees; mixed-income projects receive the waiver per affordable unit. Citywide development impact fees are deferred (as a deferral loan) for affordable units that exceed the inclusionary minimum or are built, owned and managed by HASLO, other public agencies or nonprofit housing agencies. Example: Bishop Street Studios received an impact fee deferral loan as part of $1,595,500 in City assistance; 2023 HASLO awards for 736 Orcutt and 279 Bridge Street each included a fee deferral loan. HCD's Prohousing release describes the impact fee relief as a waiver for qualifying affordable housing.
- AMI requirement: Deed-restricted affordable units at City Affordable Housing Standards (extremely low, very low, low for the fee exemption; any inclusionary-exceeding or nonprofit or public agency affordable unit for impact fee deferral).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Not applicable; requested with the building permit or through the AHF award resolution.)
- Layering notes: Local cost-reduction layer that stacks with AHF awards; the City routinely packages an AHF loan plus an impact fee deferral loan in one resolution. Fee exemptions and deferrals are public subsidies and may trigger Labor Code 1720 prevailing wage unless the project already pays it under LIHTC or state funding. The Chapter 4.56 ordinance text and current deferral terms (interest, repayment at permanent loan closing versus residual receipts) could not be opened because slocity.org, codepublishing and the City eScribe agenda host all block automated access; the HCD-hosted 2020 Housing Element incentives table is the source. No comparable county program exists for unincorporated land beyond the Title 22 incentive program.
- Source: https://www.hcd.ca.gov/housing-elements/docs/san-luis-obispo-6th-adopted072321.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Inclusionary Housing Requirements (Municipal Code Chapter 17.138, Ord. 1719, 2022) and Commercial Linkage Fee (Chapter 4.60)**
- Agency: City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department, Housing Programs
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Rental projects: 6% of units affordable (3% very low, 3% low). For-sale projects: 10% of units (5% low, 5% moderate). In-lieu fee calculated on new habitable square footage at a rate set by Council resolution in the comprehensive fee schedule; the City's inclusionary page (not opened this pass, slocity.org blocks automated access) reports about $26.73 per sq ft for-sale and $21.42 per sq ft rental, with commercial linkage fees of about $6.42 per sq ft (office, service, hotel, retail) and $5.35 per sq ft (industrial, institutional). All in-lieu and linkage fees go to the City Affordable Housing Fund. By 2020 the program had produced more than 850 affordable units and $10.45 million in in-lieu funds committed to 464 units.
- AMI requirement: Inclusionary units deed restricted 55 years rental, 45 years ownership, at City Affordable Housing Standards. Fractional units may be met by paying a fractional in-lieu fee. Exempt: ADUs and JADUs, 100% affordable projects, projects using a density bonus, downtown flexible density units (Chapter 17.141), additions and remodels that add no units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Not applicable; requirement applies at entitlement and in-lieu fee is paid before building permit issuance (phased projects pay proportionally).)
- Layering notes: Core local requirement for any market-rate multifamily deal in the City of SLO. 100% affordable projects and density bonus projects are exempt, so an LIHTC deal normally pays nothing and instead competes for the in-lieu revenue through the Affordable Housing Fund (separate record). Ordinance replaced the 1999 program in 2022 after a nexus study; the City notes Chapter 17.138 and Chapter 4.60 (nonresidential linkage fee) apply to mixed-use projects on both the residential and commercial components. County inclusionary ordinance (Title 22 Section 22.12.080) was repealed in 2022 and the County's Title 29 fund is now residual, so the City fund is the only growing in-lieu pool in the county. slocity.org returns 403 to automated access; the ordinance text was read on the zoneomics code mirror and the program history in the HCD-hosted 2020-2028 Housing Element. Confirm current fee rates on the City's inclusionary page before underwriting.
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/san-luis-obispo-CA/chapter_8
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Prohousing Designation (HCD, announced January 2024) and Prohousing Incentive Program award**
- Agency: California HCD designation; City of San Luis Obispo Community Development Department administers the incentive funds
- Type: policy/designation
- Typical award: Designation gives City-sponsored or City-located projects extra points in HCD competitive programs (AHSC, IIG, MHP and others). The City received $750,000 from the Prohousing Incentive Program in 2024, deposited to the City Affordable Housing Fund for affordable projects, with final awards to individual projects subject to Council approval. HCD lists the City (and the County, designated October 2025) among designated jurisdictions as of August 10, 2026.
- AMI requirement: Not a direct subsidy; the PIP dollars follow AHF affordability rules (55-year rental, 45-year ownership covenants).
- Cycle: rolling (next: PIP Round 5 is open to Prohousing-designated jurisdictions (the City applies, not developers) from October 13, 2026 through March 31, 2027; awards estimated June 2027. The designation benefit otherwise applies through state NOFA scoring.)
- Layering notes: Both the City and the County of San Luis Obispo are Prohousing (county record: Prohousing Designation, October 2025), so any site in the City qualifies for Prohousing bonus points in HCD programs regardless of which agency sponsors. HCD credited the City's hillside program, objective design standards and the waiver of citywide impact fees for affordable housing exceeding inclusionary requirements or built by HASLO, nonprofits or public agencies. The HCD newsroom release and designated-jurisdictions page were opened; the City's own news page about the $750,000 award could not be opened (slocity.org 403).

### City of San Mateo

**Affordable Housing Commercial Linkage Fee fund (SMMC Chapter 23.61)**
- Agency: City of San Mateo Community Development Department
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Fee on net new nonresidential construction over 5,000 square feet, adopted September 2016 (Ordinance 2016-8): office, R&D and medical office $32.76 per square foot, hotel $13.11, retail, restaurant and services $6.55 (FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27). 25% rebate for projects that sign a Standard Wage (area standard or prevailing wage) agreement; alternative of building 8 low-income units per 100,000 square feet of office, 3 per 100,000 of hotel, 1 per 100,000 of retail. Fund activity FY 2025-26: beginning $3,551,934, fees $1,090,711, loan repayments $514,717, ending balance $5,292,314 with $1,000,000 set aside for the Bespoke project and $4,000,000 programmed for housing land purchase.
- AMI requirement: Fund must support creation or preservation of housing for lower and moderate income workers; projects carry City regulatory agreements.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No NOFA. The City commits linkage fee money by Council action; the FY 2025-26 report programs $4 million toward housing land purchase. Contact housing@cityofsanmateo.org, (650) 522-7220.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. Reclassified from other to loan: the fund has deployable money and records loan repayment income ($514,717 in FY 2025-26), so it lends to affordable projects, and the five-year plan programs $4,000,000 to Housing Land Purchase (CIP 310416). After the $1,000,000 Bespoke set-aside and the $4,000,000 land purchase, only about $0.3 million of the $5,292,314 ending balance is unprogrammed, so new requests depend on future fee receipts. Pair a request with the County AHF NOFA. The City is a CDBG entitlement and joins the County HOME Consortium. Source is the FY 2025-26 Mitigation Fee Act (AB 1600) annual report; fee rates confirmed in the FY 2026-27 Comprehensive Fee Schedule.
- Source: https://www.cityofsanmateo.org/DocumentCenter/View/107918/FY2025-26-AB1600
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-07)

**Below Market Rate (BMR) inclusionary program and in-lieu fees (SMMC 27.16.050)**
- Agency: City of San Mateo Community Development Department, Neighborhood Improvement and Housing Division
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects of 11 or more units: 15% of rental units for lower income households (rents at 30% of 50% to 70% AMI, 4% annual increase cap) and 15% of ownership units for moderate income (100% to 110% AMI). Projects of 5 to 10 units and fractional units pay the BMR Housing Fee (Resolution 121 of 2008; FY 2026-27 schedule: rental $171,273 for a 5-unit project up to $342,545 for 10 units, ownership $157,187 to $314,373; fractional units $34,255 per 0.1 rental unit and $31,438 per 0.1 ownership unit). In-lieu fees are otherwise not allowed. BMR Housing Fee fund balance $254,281 at June 30, 2026 with $2,560,924 programmed for housing land purchase.
- AMI requirement: 55-year restrictions; BMR units may be up to 10% smaller than market units (20% where market units exceed 2,000 square feet); density bonus projects must provide BMR units equal to at least 15% of the base density; off-site and applicant-proposed alternatives need Council findings (Guidelines Resolution 72, June 16, 2025).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at planning application; fees indexed in the annual Comprehensive Fee Schedule each July 1. The City is a participant in the 2026 multi-city nexus study.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. San Mateo's program is unit-first: no fee option above 10 units, so inclusionary units are a given in every downtown and Hillsdale project and the City's cash sources are the Commercial Linkage Fee and the small BMR fee. Source is the adopted FY 2026-27 Comprehensive Fee Schedule (pages 11.1 to 11.2); program rules from the BMR Guidelines (cityofsanmateo.org/DocumentCenter/View/99291) and the FY 2025-26 Mitigation Fee Act report (DocumentCenter/View/107918).
- Source: https://www.cityofsanmateo.org/DocumentCenter/View/105420/Master-Fee-Schedule-26-27
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-07)


### City of San Rafael

**Affordable Housing Requirement (inclusionary), SRMC 14.16.030(B), Ordinance 1990 and Resolution 14890 guidelines, in-lieu fee set by Resolution 15179**
- Agency: City of San Rafael Community and Economic Development Department, Planning and Housing Divisions
- Type: regulatory requirement
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. In-lieu fee per required affordable unit: $396,702 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 ($389,032 in FY 2025-26, $368,274 in FY 2024-25, $362,817 in FY 2023-24), indexed annually to the California Construction Cost Index under Resolution 15179 (Dec 19, 2022). Fees are paid before building permit issuance and deposited to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund.
- AMI requirement: Primary requirement: projects of 2 to 15 units provide 10% of base units (excluding density bonus units) for low income households; projects of 15 or more units provide 5% low income. Secondary requirement for projects over 15 units: an additional 5% low income or 10% moderate income on site, or an in-lieu fee equal to 5% of base units, or off-site units within a half mile with an experienced affordable developer, or land donation appraised at or above the fee. Affordability in perpetuity, reducible to not less than 40 years on a Council finding of financial infeasibility. Fractional units below 0.5 pay the fee; 0.5 and above round up. Exempt: single-family homes, ADUs and JADUs, projects with pre-ordinance development agreements.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fee resets every July 1; FY 2027-28 figure will post after the index update. Resolution 14890 requires a program review every 3 to 5 years, so watch for amendments alongside the 2027 Housing Element mid-cycle work.)
- Layering notes: Low on-site percentages (5% to 10%) make San Rafael one of the lighter inclusionary regimes in Marin, compared with Novato's 20% and Mill Valley's 15% (25% before 2026) and the County's 20%. Developers of 100% affordable projects satisfy the requirement automatically and the City counts inclusionary units with density bonus units when they overlap, which is why in-lieu receipts have dropped (Oct 2026 staff report). The Northgate Town Square redevelopment (Merlone Geier, up to 1,422 units, entitled Dec 2, 2024, demolition began fall 2025) is the largest pipeline source of inclusionary units or fee revenue; the City pages opened state that it includes affordable housing but do not quantify the count, so confirm the development agreement terms in the Laserfiche project documents before relying on them. Fee revenue funds the Trust Fund record above. Ordinance 1990, Resolutions 14890 and 14891 were opened as PDFs on the City fees page; Resolution 15179 is on the City's Laserfiche public records portal, which refused connections this pass.
- Source: https://sanrafael.gov/affordable-housing-fees-for-developers/

- Agency: City of San Rafael Community and Economic Development Department, Housing Division (Alexis Captanian, Housing Manager, (415) 485-3383, housing@sanrafael.gov)
- Type: loan
